item.title: The US let Nvidia sell chips to an empty office in China
item.description: Concerns are being raised that neither the Commerce Department nor Nvidia are doing their due diligence when it comes to vetting Chinese firms cleared to handle the company's H200 AI chips. According to The New York Times , New Matrix is on the list of approved firms, yet its offices are empty, "a hollow gray shell with wires dangling from the ceiling where lights should be." In fact, the paper could find little evidence that the company exists in any meaningful way: Only scant information can be found online about New Matrix, which was created 17 months ago. At the building that New Matrix lists as its address, a company directory does not … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Browns season heading into Week 9 versus the Saints: Ahead of schedule good enough?
item.description: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Going into the season, the expectations around the Cleveland Browns were reasonably low . New coaching staff, the youngest roster in the league, uncertainty at the quarterback position, and the team just traded one of the best defensive players of this generation to Inglewood . Fast forward to early November, the Browns are 5-3 and are still in the playoff hunt in the AFC . Considering how many believed that around this time Cleveland would be in “making mock drafts” territory ( Editor’s Note: I did create one recently , just one), 5-3 is better than what anyone thought. As people will question how good the Browns are, it’s a fair process to go through. However, in this day and age, context is rarely used correctly. Going into the season, Cleveland had one of the easier schedules. In the first 8 games of the season, the Browns were only favored in 1 of their 5 wins, their most recent one: Week 2 @ Buccaneers: 23-19 Week 3 vs Panthers: 21-18 Week 4 vs Steelers: 27-24 Week 6 vs Ravens: 13-10 Week 7 @ Titans: 27-24 Fans’ confidence in the team has waxed and waned throughout the season, but is higher than it was before the season. If you want to argue which win was most impressive, you can make an argument that it was the home win against the Steelers. The final score doesn’t indicate how the game actually went. If you rewatched that game, the Browns looked like the better team throughout, and it was a surprise to everyone watching that night. Winning in the NFL is hard, and it doesn’t matter how you do it. Is Cleveland a good football team? Bad football team? Neither. Average, so far, but young. Offensively, despite their issues, they are better than last year. Having better personnel helps, but the scheme is better than last season. Defensively, the unit isn’t as dominant as last season, but it’s still regarded as one of the better units in the NFL. Progress is being shown even if the results aren’t as impressive. If the team were winless or 1-7, we would argue that the Browns are making any progress at all. Instead, the team is 5-3 and exceeding expectations. It’s possible that the team goes over their win total sooner rather than later , and it’s possible that the team is playing meaningful games towards mid-November and early December. How would you analyze the Browns season so far? Join the conversation! item.title: Rutgers Guard Kwabena Asamoah to Miss the Rest of the Season with Injury
item.description: PISCATAWAY, NJ - NOVEMBER 19: Rutgers Scarlet Knights offensive lineman Kwabena Asamoah (69) during the college football game between the Rutgers Scarlet Knights and the Penn State Nittany Lions on November 19, 2022 at SHI Stadium in Piscataway, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Rutgers Star guard Kwabena Asamoah will miss the rest of the season due to surgery he had for a high ankle sprain, according to 247Sports’ Bobby Deren. Asamoah, who chose to return to Rutgers for his fifth year, has played in 48 total games for the program. Unortantely due to the injury, he played his last game in a Scarlet Knight uniform as he is now out of eligibility. According to multiple reports, he is expected to make a full recovery and continue football training in January so that he is ready for the NFL Draft. Asamoah achieved several notable accolades during his Rutgers career, including being named team captain in 2026, being an All-Big Ten honorable mention in 2024 and 2025, as well as earning second-team All-America by ESPN in 2025. He also cleared the way for three 1,000-yard rushers during his career, blocking for Kyle Monangai and Antwan Raymond, who rushed for over 1,000 yards in 2023, 2024, and 2025. Through eight games of 2026, Asamoah played 498 snaps at right guard. Over that time, he allowed only three total pressures, which is tied for the fourth-fewest in the country among guards who have played at least 400 snaps. His list of consecutive starts was one of the longest on the team, as he started every game in 2024, 2025, and the first eight games in 2026. With his college career now over, Asamoah will look to recover quickly and prepare for the NFL Draft. In addition to Asamoah being ruled out for the season, star wide receiver KJ Duff has been ruled out for the Knights’ upcoming game against Wisconsin. His injury has been deemed a lower-body injury, but specifics have not been released. Last week, Duff left the game against Michigan early due to the injury. These two, combined with starting quarterback Dylan Lonergan being out for the game, mean that Rutgers will be taking on Wisconsin without several key pieces on offense.

item.title: Tottenham dealt latest attacking injury blow after VAR madness at Leeds
item.description: Tottenham have been dealt another attacking injury blow after Mathys Tel limped off before half-time against Leeds . Tel was unable to continue after being on the end of a stamp by Jayden Bogle, who caught the Frenchman on the ankle with his studs. VAR spent over four minutes reviewing the incident to determine whether it was a red card offence, only for referee John Brooks - who didn’t even caution Bogle initially - to be told to stick with the on-field decision. This meant the right wing-back got away with the challenge scot free. “The referee’s call of no red card to Bogle for the challenge on Tel was checked and confirmed by VAR,” said the Premier League Match Centre. Should Jason Bogle have seen red for this challenge? 🟥👀 📺 Stream live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/fuK42Okkcz — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 7, 2026 The statement added VAR Tony Harrington’s verdict to Brooks: “I'm confirming the on-field decision of no red card. There’s a lack of speed going into the challenge and he’s stepping into the tackle. Confirming a reckless challenge”. The challenge was similar to the one that saw Jean-Philippe Mateta shown red after a VAR review when Spurs played Crystal Palace last weekend. Spurs manager Roberto De Zerbi was visibly frustrated with the outcome of the review and expressed his displeasure again when Pedro Porro was booked for a similar foul after the break, with the Italian booked for his reaction. Roberto De Zerbi was booked for his reaction after Pedro Porro was cautioned for a similar tackle to Jayden Bogle’s (Reuters) “Pedro Porro's was a duel and an incredible yellow card. The first situation of Mathys Tel I didn't see, I can't say nothing,” De Zerbi told TNT Sports , before stopping short of criticising the officials. Asked if the referee should have gone to the monitor to review Bogle’s challenge, he said: "No. I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to the monitor. If they didn't take the right decision I don't know. We have to keep the eyes on the performance where can improve." De Zerbi’s woes were exacerbated when Tel signalled to the bench that he would need to come off, having tried to play through the pain for five minutes. Tel was replaced by Dominic Solanke in the 43rd minute, who was dropped from the starting line-up following the Palace win. Mathys Tel was forced off during Tottenham's clash with Leeds (Getty) De Zerbi’s attacking options have already been ravaged by injury this season and the club will now be left to sweat over the extent of Tel’s setback. Savio and Mykhailo Mudryk are out until after the international break, while Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert are continuing to work their way back from serious knee injuries, with both eyeing returns after the turn of the year. Tel has impressed for Spurs in recent weeks, scoring a stunning solo goal in their 2-0 win over Chelsea on 24 October, the club’s first victory at Stamford Bridge

item.title: Maryvale football wins first playoff game in 21 years
item.description: For the first time in 21 years, the Maryvale Panthers have won a playoff game. No. 13 Phoenix Maryvale shut out the No. 20 ALA West Foothills Guardians, 35-0, in a first-round 4A high school football playoff game on Friday, Nov. 6. The Panthers used a stifling defense to secure three takeaways and consistently give the offense a short field. Key Plays The Panthers scored their first touchdown of the game when freshman quarterback Marcus Escobedo Jr. found Miles Woods for a 14-yard score with 5:16 to go in the first. Maryvale junior running back Isaac Buchanan scored the first of his two touchdowns after a 25-yard run reached pay dirt with 7:15 to go in the second quarter. Escobedo Jr. found the end zone after a nifty red zone scramble and crossed the pylon with just seconds before the first half ended, putting the Panthers up 21-0. Buchanan scored the final touchdown of the game scoring from a yard out after a 35-yard catch and run from Woods set them up with a goal to go at the 1 yardline. Key Players Maryvale's Escobedo Jr. finished the game throwing for 209 yards and a touchdown on 11 of 15 passing. He also added a rushing touchdown. Woods caught five passes for 135 yards and a touchdown, averaging a whopping 27 yards a catch in Friday's contest. Junior RB Buchanan had a workhorse performance rushing for 67 yards on 16 carries and scoring two touchdowns. Quotes "Tonight we blanked a really good football team," Maryvale co-head coach Marcus Carter said. "We're physical, we're fast, we're young and these kids are sponges and they're hungry. To pitch a shutout against a really good ALA west team is a statement." "Our freshman QB has poise," Maryvale co-head coach Mark Carter said. "He could have gone to any school, he decided to come here, we feel blessed to have him and he's only going to get better." "We just couldn't get that spark," ALA West Foothill head coach Bryan Rauzen said. "We're going to miss these seniors a lot but I can positively say we are building a tradition here." Up next Maryvale (10-1) will travel to Prescott, to face No. 4 Bradshaw Mountain (7-3) in the second round on Nov. 13. The Bears had a first-round bye. The season ended Friday for ALA West Foothills. This article originally appeared on Arizona Republic: Maryvale football wins first playoff game in 21 years

item.title: Mainz 05 vs. Bayern Munich: Gamethread
item.description: Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images | Getty Images 46’ — The second half is a go! Halftime Observations Bayern hasn’t been entirely bad in this half. The team mostly did what they had to do but some brilliant phases by Mainz ensured Bayern weren’t going to steamroller them. Is something wrong with Kane? He can’t score and almost always lays the ball off instead of going for goal himself. That VAR decision to rule out Mainz’s goal is down to interpretation, but the fact is Bayern can’t rely on close calls like that to get the win. They’ll need more than that to win. Speaking of: it makes no difference if the mistake on Mainz’s goal is blamed on Jonathan Tah or Manuel Neuer, but the fact is Neuer can’t play full games like he used to. The guy’s body can’t handle it anymore ever since the foot injuries stretching back to almost a decade ago. 45+7’ — Halftime. 45+3’ — Josip Stanišić shoots from the left side but misses the target. 45’ — NO GOAL! A lengthy VAR check confirms Mainz’s goal was offside. Manuel Neuer is also off for Jonas Urbig due to foot problems from the former. Six minutes of stoppage time is also added on. 40’ — Goal. Neuer’s poor punch lands at Lee’s path and heads the equalizer in. 37’ — Karl plays Kane through but he came too close to Zentner and couldn’t get a good shot off. 36’ — Kane tries his luck from distance but the ball goes high over the goal. 27’ — Manuel Neuer rushes out to clear a ball, then watched the incoming Mainz cross reach no one. 23’ — Kimmich’s corner comes to nothing for Bayern. 17-18’ — Nathaniel Brown snuck in behind the defense and his attempt gets saved. Moments later, Dayot Upamecano had a header saved. 14’ — TOR! Danny Da Costa misses Lee Jae-sung’s backwards pass outside their box, which allowed Harry Kane to lay off to Joshua Kimmich who fired into the top corner. Bayern leads 1-0! 12’ — Michael Olise just misses out on a forward ball from outside the box. 9’ — Bayern wins a corner and it falls to Lennart Karl, who does his best to keep away from the Mainz defenders but his shot is not enough to beat Robin Zentner. 7’ — Bayern evade the Mainz press but Nathaniel Brown misses the pass into the box. 3’ — Bayern on the back foot in the opening stretch of the match. Kickoff! — LET’S GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO!!!!! Lineups are out! Bayern fields a strong starting XI to take on Mainz. Aleksandar Pavlović marks his return to the starting XI, relegating Tom Bischof to the bench. Nathaniel Brown starts today, presumably on the left wing, while Alphonso Davies starts as a substitute. item.title: MLS Decision Day Rondo: Can Nashville SC make history? Will LA Galaxy and the Seattle Sounders avoid playoff disaster?
item.description: MLS winners and losers GFX - GOAL A points record within reach, seasons on the brink and star names under pressure: GOAL’s writers debate who will rise - and who could fall - on MLS Decision Day. Right, so, Decision Day time. For those uninitiated, this is basically where all of the MLS games kick off at the same time on the final day of the regular season. In an ideal world, there are still loads of possible permutations and combinations as to who makes the playoffs and how. Decision Day is supposed to be, well, decisive. And this year, it might just be lacking a bit of spark. The East, from a 'who makes it' POV is sewn up. The West has a little wildcard jeopardy, but basically we're looking at one or two sides falling out of the picture late on. However, there is some drama to be found. Nashville SC tied the single-season points record last week. Any sort of result against FC Cincinnati on Saturday, and they will set a new one. And even if the West isn't all that pumping, having a number of games kick off at the same time means things will fluctuate throughout the night. So, what does this all look like? And does this year's Decision Day feel as decisive as it should? GOAL writers break it down in another edition of... The Rondo . Will Nashville SC set a points record this weekend? Hany Mukhtar has been magnificent in Nashville's record-breaking season. Tom Hindle : Why not?! Sure, after securing the Supporters' Shield and tying a record, B.J. Callaghan might be tempted to rest some of his guys and make sure nothing goes too wrong. But their opponent, FC Cincinnati, are more or less locked where they're at. The smart money, based on this season? Nashville concede and then mount a furious late comeback. Alex Labidou: It’s been a regular season of destiny for the Boys in Gold , so why would that change on Decision Day? I fully expect Nashville to finish the job Saturday and claim the points record. Ryan Tolmich: It’ll be tough considering Cincinnati will have something to play for. Even so, Nashville are the best team in MLS, so it would be silly to bet against them. Which two Western Conference teams will secure wild card slots? Brian Schmetzer's Seattle Sounders shouldn't be counted out in the West playoff hunt TH : Wow, it's tight. But let's assume the results shake out in the way they should , and it will be Seattle and Colorado in a wildcard slot, with LA Galaxy sliding in at seventh place. Minnesota United have been magnificent of late, but they will need help from elsewhere, and San Jose are a tough opponent. No miracle for the Loons . AL: This is tough, but it’s hard to imagine Brian Schmetzer and the Seattle Sounders missing the playoffs. I’m banking on the Rave Green to secure one spot. While Colorado and the LA Galaxy have more talent than Portland, the Timbers have the most favorable Decision Day matchup: a hapless Austin FC side sitting 14th. On that basis, I’m backing Portland to get in, too. RT: The odds are heavily against Seattle

item.title: Hamilton, Leclerc and Verstappen to have penalties
item.description: Lewis Hamilton and Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc will both have 10-place grid penalties in Sao Paulo on Sunday [Getty Images] Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will all have grid penalties at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Verstappen will start from the back of the grid while Hamilton and Leclerc will both have 10-place penalties. They join Mercedes driver George Russell in having penalties for using too many engine parts. Russell's drop is only five places. Verstappen will have an an all-new engine fitted after Red Bull discovered problems after Friday practice. Leclerc, Hamilton and Russell have all fitted new internal combustion engines. The penalties for the Ferrari drivers are bigger than Russell's because it is the first time they have exceeded the limit of four engines per season, while Russell had already gone beyond that. Verstappen famously won the 2024 Sao Paulo Grand Prix from 17th on the grid after an engine penalty in a wet race. Rain is predicted overnight from Saturday into Sunday in the city this year, with forecasts saying it could rain at any point on race day. Meanwhile, F1 announced on Saturday that Sao Paulo's Interlagos circuit had extended its contract to host a grand prix until 2035. F1 president and chief executive officer Stefano Domenicali said: "Brazil is an important part of F1's history and our future, and I am delighted that this five-year extension will see us continue racing in Sao Paulo until 2035. "The passion of our Brazilian fans is extraordinary, and every time we return to Interlagos we feel their energy in the grandstands and in the city of Sao Paulo. "The continued success and excitement surrounding the event shows why it holds such a special place on our calendar, and this agreement underlines our long-term commitment to Brazil." item.title: F1 Brazilian GP: Max Verstappen edges out Kimi Antonelli in FP3
item.description: Motorsport photo Max Verstappen set the fastest time in Free Practice 3 at Formula 1’s Brazilian Grand Prix, narrowly edging out Kimi Antonelli as Lewis Hamilton ’s Ferrari suffered a mechanical issue. The impending threat of rain meant all drivers rushed onto the track – especially Nico Hulkenberg , whose Audi suffered a terminal issue at the hands of rookie Freddie Slater in FP1, preventing him from partaking in the second session at all. These laps were therefore the German’s first this weekend. Everyone focused on the medium tyre compound in the opening 40 minutes of the session, Kimi Antonelli fastest in 1m12.209s, leading Verstappen by 0.075s – despite the new world champion reporting a steering wheel problem, while the four-time title winner reported his steering was “heavy to the right”. Charles Leclerc was third, 0.230s adrift, while George Russell , Liam Lawson and Oscar Piastri were half a second down on Antonelli. Lawson, who set the fastest time in sector three, was nearly 0.5s quicker than Racing Bulls team-mate Arvid Lindblad and almost one second faster than any other midfield driver. Hamilton, who reported “strange vibrations” emanating from his new powertrain and “big engine braking”, was just eighth-fastest ahead of Hadjar, who described his RB22 as “close to undriveable”. The Ferrari man’s issue would later lead to “smoke in the cockpit” amid a worrying sound. As the field switched to soft rubber, Verstappen narrowly edged out Antonelli to set the fastest time, with a 1m11.622s to the Mercedes driver’s 1m11.647s. Lando Norris hauled his McLaren up to third, 0.131s adrift, followed by Russell and Leclerc – meaning the four top teams lapped within 0.274s. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes This time, Lindblad was one tenth quicker than Lawson, with the pair again roughly half a second faster than Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto and Alpine ’s Pierre Gasly in the midfield. Hadjar also ended up behind both Racing Bulls in the classification, with a 0.591s deficit to pacesetter Verstappen. Hamilton’s issue meant he was confined to the garage and performed no soft-tyre run, ending up 12th in the final results. Debutant Rafael Camara was 15th-fastest, 0.128s quicker than team-mate Oliver Bearman . Lance Stroll propped up the order after encountering a suspected ERS issue 15 minutes into the session, which proved terminal. item.title: Former Real Madrid star opines on Vinicius’ situation: ‘They play better with Diomande’
item.description: Former Real Madrid star opines on Vinicius’ situation: ‘They play better with Diomande’ Vinicius Jr.’s spot in Real Madrid’s starting XI is now under serious threat, or, for practical purposes, may well be gone. The long-term suspension has not helped the player’s case in any way after his poor start to the season. Some saw it as a much-needed reset for the Brazilian star, but as he prepared to return to league action after the international break, he will find Yan Diomande sitting comfortably ahead of him as Jose Mourinho’s preferred option on the left wing. Former player speaks on Vinicius Former Real Madrid and Spain striker Fernando Morientes spoke to the media earlier this week, where he opened up with his honest assessment of Vinicius Jr.’s situation and his competition with Yan Diomande. Tough times for Vinicius Jr. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Sharing his honest thoughts on the same, Morientes admitted that Vinicius was not quite at the level that he is usually associated with, as he said (h/t Defensa Central ): “We are not looking at the best version of Vinicius at the moment, but, well, that is the reality. I think he himself has acknowledged it, hasn’t he?” He then stressed that it was the responsibility of the coaching staff to ensure the player returns to his best. “The responsibility of the coaching staff, without getting into the wider debate, is to try to bring back the best version of Vinicius,” he began. “Especially considering that his current performances have fallen short of what is expected from a player of his stature, given his history at Real Madrid and his most recent contract renewal,” he added. “The coaching staff’s job is to work towards that without fuelling all the external debate surrounding him,” he concluded. Morientes then backed Yan Diomande as Real Madrid’s superior left-wing option at this point in time. Diomande has utilised his chances well. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) “The reality today is that Diomande is in better form, and Real Madrid currently play better with Diomande on the left than they do with Vinicius. “At the same time, however, the coaching staff’s responsibility is to bring back Vinicius’s best version.” On what lies ahead for Vinicius The former striker then backed Vinicius to come good and insisted that he is still a decent player who can contribute, even until he returns to his best. “I believe he is a player who can still contribute. I believe he is an important player, and I don’t think we should write him off, because players like him can be decisive when they are in top form.” “When a player like Vinicius, whose strengths are taking on defenders, dribbling and scoring goals, fails to deliver those qualities, his shortcomings become much more noticeable than those of other players,” he added. item.title: NBC solicits Brent Musburger, Bob Costas to narrate opening tease for Miami-Notre Dame
item.description: Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NBC Sports is giving Saturday’s Miami-Notre Dame matchup the big-game treatment with one of the network’s famous pregame teases. Before the Hurricanes and Fighting Irish kick off from South Bend at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC, the network will give viewers a brief history of the recently renewed rivalry in the trademark style NBC Sports is known for. The opening tease begins with clips of Jimmy Johnson’s and Lou Holtz’s Miami and Notre Dame teams at the inception of what is now colloquially known as Catholics vs. Convicts before transitioning to the modern day, when a three-point Miami win in Week 1 of the 2025 season proved to be the difference between which team earned the final bid into the College Football Playoff just a year ago. And to add to the stakes, NBC has tapped two heavyweights to narrate the package. Brent Musburger, who called the original Catholics vs. Convicts game for CBS in 1988, narrates the tease alongside Bob Costas, who has lent his voice to many of NBC’s trademark opens throughout his time with the network. NBC has leaned into its history of producing narrative-setting opens for big games of late, particularly since the NBA returned to its airwaves last year. Many associate the style of these packages, and Costas’ voice, with Michael Jordan’s Chicago Bulls dynasty in the ’90s, and NBC Sports dutifully brought them back last NBA season to heaping praise. Now, the network will go back to the well for what is arguably the biggest college football game it will air all season. item.title: Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc hit with Sao Paulo grid penalties in more Ferrari misery
item.description: Warring Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will both receive 10-place grid penalties for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix . The Ferrari duo have both changed their engines for the first time this season and as such have been hit with the penalty by the FIA. The pair held showdown talks with boss Fred Vasseur on Thursday evening after Hamilton’s fury over his team-mate’s lap-one overtake on him in Mexico. Lewis Hamilton drives past a mural of Ayrton Senna in Sao Paulo (Bradley Collyer/PA) Hamilton questioned Leclerc’s mentality and vowed not to be silenced at Ferrari as he arrived in Brazil. Vasseur and Leclerc say the matter is settled after those talks. Their squabble allowed Max Verstappen to win last weekend’s race. The Dutchman has risen to second in the standings after victory in three of the last four races but will start from the rear of the grid on Sunday after taking on several new engine components. It is a position he is familiar with having done the same here over the last two years, famously winning from 17th in the rain in 2024. Rain fell as final practice got under way on Saturday and is forecast across the weekend, with the chance of qualifying and Sunday’s race being affected. Formula One announced a five-year extension for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix ahead of qualifying, confirming its place on the calendar until 2035.

item.title: Are the Badgers right to make a QB change to Ryan Hopkins?
item.description: MADISON, WI - SEPTEMBER 12: Wisconsin quarterback Ryan Hopkins (10) hands the ball off to Wisconsin running back Bryan Jackson II (21) during a college football game between the University of Wisconsin Badgers and the Western Illinois University Leathernecks on September 12, 2026, at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, WI. (Photo by Lawrence Iles/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers are finally making a change at quarterback, as Ryan Hopkins will get his first career start against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights, and looks to have the green light for Wisconsin’s final four games of the season. The Badgers, sitting at 5-3, have really struggled to throw the ball with starter Colton Joseph, who has completed under 56 percent of his passes this season, and has gone for fewer than 100 passing yards in three straight outings. The roughest one came last weekend against the Iowa Hawkeyes, as Joseph completed just 5 of 14 passes before being benched for Hopkins for the fourth quarter. Coming out of that game, Hopkins remains the starter, which a majority of fans looked for in our weekly Reacts poll. Wisconsin now faces Rutgers, Maryland, Purdue, and Minnesota in its final four games, so it should get an accurate look at Hopkins before making a key quarterback decision for the 2027 season. Was this the right time to make the quarterback change? Just a week ago, we saw reports that Wisconsin was negotiating with Colton Joseph for the 2027 season. But now, that feels unlikely, and it comes down to a rough transfer portal evaluation. Joseph just never improved the way the Badgers wanted him to, as accuracy and footwork issues were prevalent from the offseason and have carried throughout the year. He was a major work in progress coming into the season with his passing inconsistencies at Old Dominion, but his rushing ability was expected to provide a quality floor in the Big Ten. Still, Wisconsin’s offense has struggled a good amount, and moving to Hopkins feels like a much-needed move here at the end of the season. With jobs at stake, Wisconsin needs to see if Hopkins can be its guy next season or whether it’ll need to evaluate outside the program for its starter next year. At the very least, Hopkins looked confident as a passer last week, while dealing with some rookie mistakes. If he can build on that, Wisconsin has a chance to finish this season strong. It all starts on Saturday, when the Badgers take on Rutgers as 19.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel. But it’s another missed quarterback evaluation for the Badgers, and one that should create a lot of questions on process in the offseason.

item.title: Chris Bosh says change that has been made throughout the NBA was ‘definitely a mistake’
item.description: Photo by Steve Marcus/Getty Images Chris Bosh believes the lack of preseason games has been one of the reasons behind the rise of injuries in the NBA. The Hall of Famer played 70 or more games eight times in his career, which is a sensational achievement. In the current NBA, with injuries rising, not a lot of people are able to compete in a large number of games. Already, players like Tyrese Haliburton, Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace, Anthony Edwards and Paolo Banchero are set to miss months due to injuries, which has led to an outcry among many to reduce the number of games per season. There has been no decision regarding the number of games being reduced, but the belief is that Adam Silver could be interested in trimming the game down to 40 minutes. No guarantee that playing fewer minutes will completely take away injuries, but Bosh knows what has led to the rise in injuries. Chris Bosh speaks on the importance of preseason The number of preseason games has reduced significantly in the past few years. CBA rules suggest that teams will not be allowed to play more than six preseason games. Despite this, very few teams use the full quota, and on average, franchises just give their players 3 to 5 games in the preseason. “I saw something really interesting over the weekend on RJ’s podcast, and he was speaking of how guys, especially the superstar guys, right? The guys who the team have paid them all their money to lead them, to score all the points, get all the rebounds, be the superstars that they are. And we expect these guys, going from a short training camp, only playing about one or two preseason games, to playing big minutes at a higher level, faster level, once the regular season starts. And that’s definitely a mistake,” said Bosh in a video that he uploaded online. “Before, we had eight preseason games. Maybe eight’s too much. I don’t know. But one thing that was for certain was that you were going to get in basketball shape, and even getting used to the movements, getting used to contact.” Richard Jefferson blasted the modern NBA players for not taking training seriously for the regular season and avoiding preseason. He used his own example to show how players today were not preparing well and jumping straight into the regular season, leading to a rise in injuries. “I do believe, watching Jalen Williams’ injury, it was really, really tough to watch. I have to think if they had more practice time, if they had more preseason games, would his body have more balance, you know, and be able to take more contact in the air like that? And, you know, he still did land awkward, but I have to believe that playing more basketball gets you used to the basketball movements, used to taking contact, and it just gets you used to the overall pounding that your body has to take,” he added. “We felt that we had to get, you know, condition our bodies, get in shape first, get used to that contact, so then we could be able to go out and perform the games. item.title: ‘Haven’t Completely Abandoned the Idea’ — NFL Insiders Reveal NFC Team’s Stance on Potentially Adding Brandon Aiyuk
item.description: ‘Haven’t Completely Abandoned the Idea’ — NFL Insiders Reveal NFC Team’s Stance on Potentially Adding Brandon Aiyuk Brandon Aiyuk’s future with the San Francisco 49ers remains uncertain as the NFL trade deadline approaches. With Washington still considering the wide receiver, ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport have shared a fresh update on the Commanders’ stance, with injuries to its receiving corps potentially keeping the door open for a deal. Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport Reveal Commanders’ Stance on Brandon Aiyuk According to a joint report from ESPN’s Schefter and NFL Network’s Rapoport, Washington is still considering the possibility of acquiring the 28-year-old receiver. “The Commanders haven’t completely abandoned the idea of adding wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, who was rumored during the summer to end up in Washington, according to sources,” Schefter and Rapoport reported . “But before an Aiyuk deal were to happen, if it were to happen, the organization would have to have discussions with multiple people. It’s not a no, but it’s also not a yes just yet.” The Commanders, ranked 26th overall with a 69.2 grade on PFN’s NFL Team Overall Impact , have several reasons to consider the move. They are 2-4-1 and third in the NFC East, with injuries creating major problems for their passing game. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator Terry McLaurin has been ruled out for the season after suffering a torn patellar tendon. Meanwhile, Treylon Burks and Dyami Brown have also dealt with injury setbacks. Adding Aiyuk could give Washington another experienced receiver, but the organization would need to carefully consider his situation before making a move. Aiyuk’s Reinstatement Push Adds Another Layer to the Situation Aiyuk’s future with the 49ers remains uncertain after a lengthy dispute with the organization. The receiver has not played since suffering serious knee injuries, including a torn ACL and MCL, in October 2024. His relationship with San Francisco deteriorated following contract disagreements and a prolonged hold-in. The 49ers eventually voided $27 million in guaranteed money for 2026 and placed him on the reserve/left squad list after he stopped participating in team activities. Aiyuk recently hired prominent agent Drew Rosenhaus and filed paperwork seeking reinstatement to the NFL. The move has put pressure on San Francisco to determine his future, whether through a trade, release, or another resolution. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Aiyuk and Rosenhaus met with 49ers officials at the team’s business offices in Santa Clara on Friday, November 6. However, the meeting ended without an immediate resolution. Rosenhaus offered a brief “To be continued” when asked about the situation, leaving Aiyuk’s next move unclear. item.title: 😅 A mixed blessing?! Neuer's record match goes horribly wrong
item.description: 😅 A mixed blessing?! Neuer's record match goes horribly wrong By starting in Bayern's Bundesliga match against Mainz 05 today, Manuel Neuer overtook Bernd Dreher as FC Bayern's oldest-ever Bundesliga player. At 40 years and 225 days, he is now the oldest player to represent the record champions in the Bundesliga. And at first, everything went to plan. Kimmich put Bayern ahead in Mainz after 14 minutes, with Kane providing the assist. Then, in the 40th minute, things slowly but surely started going downhill, especially for record-breaker Manuel Neuer. Amiri swung a free kick into the box. Tah slightly deflected the delivery towards the far post, Neuer came flying out and missed it by a mile, and Jae-Sung Lee tapped in behind him for what appeared to be the equaliser. Immediately after his ill-fated and unsuccessful leap, Neuer signalled that something was wrong. After receiving treatment on his right foot, he had to come off, with Jonas Urbig replacing him. So Neuer is injured again, but there was still a silver lining. His mistake in misjudging the free kick went unpunished. Lee was narrowly offside when he scored, and after a VAR check, the goal was disallowed, leaving Bayern ahead at the break. What do you think of the incident? Let us know in the comments! This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇩🇪 here.

item.title: NFL trade deadline 2026: Denver Broncos latest news and rumors
item.description: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks at the scoreboard during the second quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 2 p.m. MT, and our Denver Broncos could be an active team prior to the deadline. They have been widely connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor in the days leading up to the deadline , but according to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the team could explore adding a weapon or two to their offense. He mentions running back, tight end, and wide receiver as the positions that they could add. With Harvey injury and Badie also on IR and injuries across the offense, would expect Broncos to explore adding a weapon or two before trade deadline (RB, TE, WR). https://t.co/TSad3tJ2d3 — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) October 31, 2026 Looking at the Broncos’ needs heading into the deadline, the most glaring one is running back. Now, the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman helps, but the Broncos still need more from the position. RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie are on the injured reserve, and veteran JK Dobbins has been struggling all season. So, adding another back to pair with Coleman would make sense. The question is, will they go big and add a Jonathan Taylor or Breece Hall? Or make a smaller move for someone like Tony Pollard or someone else? Klis mentions wide receiver, and while it may not be the most pressing need right now, it could be in a few months. Jaylen Waddle has not performed as expected thus far; Courtland Sutton will be 32 next season and has a large cap hit(Also restructured his deal and could be off the team next season); Pat Bryant has been very good, but has been on the IR; Marvin Mims is a pending free agent, while Troy Franklin is buried on the depth chart. Could the Broncos be looking to add a wide receiver who could contribute to this team this season and moving forward? This doesn’t seem as likely, but I wouldn’t rule it out if the right deal comes their way. As for tight end, I don’t know. The only name that could move the needle and that might be available is Dallas Goedert, but is that even worth it? He would certainly improve that room, but the Broncos really do not utilize their tight ends in the passing game. Evan Engram has had a disappointing year, and blocking specialist Nate Adkins leads the group (and, funny enough, the team) in TD receptions with 3, but he only has 6 total catches thus far. We’ll be tracking all the Broncos news and rumors throughout the weekend and right up to the deadline. It’s supposed to be an active deadline, so we’ll see if our Denver Broncos make any splashes or not in the coming days. Some notable trade Candidates Colts RB Jonathan Taylor Colts WR Josh Downs Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr. Titans RB Tony Pollard Eagles TE Dallas Goedert Chargers EDGE Khalil Mack Cardin

item.title: Wrexham owners' presence uplifting - Parkinson
item.description: Ryan Reynolds (left) and Rob Mac (right) took control of Wrexham in February 2021 [Getty Images] Phil Parkinson says the presence of co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac at Wrexham's draw with Wolverhampton Wanderers once again gave the club a significant lift. The Hollywood duo were in attendance as Lewis O'Brien's first goal of the campaign earned the Red Dragons a 1-1 draw following Adam Armstrong's opener at the Racecourse Ground. Following the draw, Parkinson stated everyone connected to the club is lifted when the duo attend a home fixture. "It's always very uplifting, I feel, for the people who work at the club, first of all, the players and the staff when Rob and Ryan come over," he said. "The crowd as well, they're uplifted by the owners being in town. "I communicate with them when they're back in the States, but equally it's good to have a chat with them when they're over." Wrexham claim point against in-form Wolves Wrexham chief executive Williamson leaves after two years The draw means Wrexham have claimed four points from their matches with promotion-hopefuls Middlesbrough and Wolves this week on the back of what was a disappointing 1-0 loss to Sheffield United last weekend. Following the defeat by the Blades, Parkinson raised concerns over the lack of a "Wrexham feel" to the display , something they rectified in fine fashion by beating Boro five days later. Having ensured they go into the final international window of 2026 in positive spirits, Parkinson stated the presence of Reynolds and Mac in north Wales has once again helped to highlight the importance of togetherness at the club. "Whatever division we've been in, when Rob and Ryan have been here, I think it's good for the players to see their connection with the club, how much they care and how much they're watching from afar," added the Wrexham manager. "Since day one we've been in it together. I always say that when we've done well and have got promoted, how everybody at this club has got this enormous togetherness and that starts from the very top." item.title: Tinubu-Shettima ticket most formidable in Nigeria’s history, says APC chair
item.description: The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nentawe Yilwatda, has described the presidential ticket of President Bola Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima as the most formidable in Nigeria’s political history, urging Nigerians to support their re-election in 2027. Yilwatda said Tinubu deserved another term to consolidate the economic reforms and infrastructure projects initiated by his administration. He made the remarks on Saturday at the Rainbow Coalition Presidential Campaign Rally held at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. In a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Media and Information Strategy, Abimbola Tooki, the APC chairman said the Tinubu-Shettima ticket combined political experience, courage and leadership capacity needed to address the country’s challenges. “The most formidable presidential ticket we have ever produced in Nigeria is the Tinubu-Shettima ticket. We have a candidate in President Bola Ahmed Tinubu who is fearless, courageous and determined to confront the challenges of our country. He has demonstrated the capacity to take difficult decisions in the national interest, and he has remained resolute in pursuing the transformation of Nigeria,” he said. Yilwatda defended the administration’s economic policies, including the removal of the petrol subsidy and the unification of the foreign exchange market, describing them as necessary steps towards rebuilding the economy and strengthening public finances. Although he acknowledged that the reforms had created difficulties for households and businesses, he said the government was working to cushion their effects through economic stabilisation measures, social interventions and infrastructure investments. The APC chairman also praised Tinubu’s infrastructure programme, particularly major highway projects, which he said would improve connectivity, facilitate trade and create economic opportunities. “We have a President who understands that development cannot happen without infrastructure. He has initiated an ambitious infrastructure revolution through major highway projects that will connect different parts of Nigeria, open up economic corridors, facilitate the movement of goods and services and create new opportunities for our people,” Yilwatda said. He urged Nigerians to support the continuation of the administration’s policies, arguing that a second term would allow Tinubu to consolidate the reforms and deliver their expected benefits. Turning to Rivers State, Yilwatda commended political leaders and members of the Rainbow Coalition for supporting Tinubu’s re-election bid across party lines. He said the growing political cooperation in the state reflected a shared commitment to national development, irrespective of party affiliation. “Come 2027, we want to continue with this reformer and performer as our President. That is why the coalition and the people of Rivers State, irrespective of political party, have decided to work

item.title: UK Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch says Trump deserved midterm defeat
item.description: British Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has said United States President Donald Trump deserved to be defeated in the midterm elections, describing the setback as “entirely self-inflicted.” In an interview with The Independent , Badenoch criticised Trump’s handling of the Iran war, his trade policies and his treatment of allies. She said his approach did not reflect conservative principles. The Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday’s midterms, flipping at least seven Senate seats and more than two dozen House districts in a major blow to Trump’s Republican Party. Asked whether Trump deserved the defeat, Badenoch replied: “Yeah. He has not been acting in the way that I would consider conservative.” She condemned his tariffs, threats towards Canada and Greenland, and disputes with allies, saying they contradicted the conservative emphasis on free markets and better trade. “Where is the push for free markets and better trade… rather than protectionism, America first, the squabbling with allies? That’s not what conservatives do,” she said. Badenoch also criticised Trump’s personal attacks on journalists and political figures, stating that his conduct fell short of the standards expected of a statesman. “Trump is very charming in person, but you see the way that he talks about journalists, about individuals. It doesn’t meet the standards a statesman should meet – always wanting to get dirty in terms of insults and so on,” she said. She expressed particular unhappiness with Trump’s remarks about British Prime Minister Keir Starmer and described his treatment of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at the White House as “awful.” On the Iran conflict, Badenoch said she understood and supported Trump’s initial decision to take military action due to concerns about Iran acquiring nuclear weapons, but questioned the lack of a clear strategy. “We don’t want them getting nuclear weapons. But where’s the plan?” she asked. Badenoch added that she would have been content if Trump had lost the 2024 presidential election to Kamala Harris. When asked which of the two candidates she preferred, she said: “I would say I like them both equally. Make of that what you will.” She further argued that Trump had squandered the broad coalition of voters that helped him win the presidency, including increased support from Latino and Black voters. “What’s the first thing he does? Tariffs, and then talking about Greenland and Canada. A lot of people were wondering, ‘What are you doing?’” she said. Badenoch became leader of the UK Conservative Party and Leader of the Opposition in November 2024. Born Olukemi Olufunto Adegoke in London in 1980 to Nigerian parents, she previously served as Business and Trade Secretary under former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak. The post UK Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch says Trump deserved midterm defeat appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
item.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments." item.title: AI broke the cybersecurity world. What’s next?
item.description: Today, I’m talking with Alex Stamos, chief security officer at Cognition and longtime cybersecurity expert, about what a mess cybersecurity is right now. This episode is part one of a special series looking at AI in real life. I’ve always enjoyed talking to Alex because he’s so direct, and you’re going to hear him say that the multibillion-dollar cybersecurity industry as we’ve known it is essentially overdue to the unrelenting, AI-boosted waves of hacks, breaches, and attacks — and this is only the beginning of how much AI is changing security. Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here . Not a subscriber? You can sign up here . Both private actors and also state actors, like Russia or North Korea, are breaking into systems all over thanks to AI helping them both detect and exploit vulnerabilities all at the same time. It’s got a real frontier feel to it, Alex notes, just like the ’90s, when the whole idea of an always-online world was brand-new. That much disruption means a lot of places where bad guys can get in while everyone else is left scrambling. Alex isn’t a doomer in the long run, but he does think we’re in for a “dark age” while we try to figure out how on earth to adapt to the new era. There’s a lot going on here — we even got all the way to how AI-powered misinformation and slop might be managed on our social networks. Before we get going, do me a favor and subscribe to Decoder on YouTube, where we put out new episodes every Monday and Thursday. Okay: Alex Stamos on how AI is upending cybersecurity. Here we go. Welcome back to Decoder . Hey, thanks for having me, man. I’m excited to talk to you. It’s been a long time since you and I chatted in what you might call the “content moderation era” of internet policy discourse. I feel like you and I talked a lot about how all that was working, about election security, all those sorts of things. We’re in a new era of big problems on the internet, particularly around cyber defense, cybersecurity. You’ve been thinking about this stuff a lot. What’s been less discussed is a huge number of companies have been breached. You have a series of AI-related companies, the neoclouds that have been breached in succession. item.title: Fireworks says you’re wasting money on AI unless you’re using all the models
item.description: Fireworks AI is fine with helping companies run AI models in their own datacenters, though VP Rob Ferguson argues against doing so. Ferguson told The Register in an interview that while Fireworks AI, a managed inference provider, supports on-prem AI, "we're trying to push people more and more away from it because frankly, it's just the economics." The GPU hardware is just so expensive that if you can't keep it fully utilized, it's a waste of money, he contends. Ten thousand GPUs, he said, represent a billion dollars of capital. "You don't want those things to be sitting idle," he said. For companies with particularly sensitive workloads, Ferguson said, Fireworks is happy to work something out – it offers a service called Sovereign for just that purpose and it has partners like Microsoft that can help. But most inference work probably doesn't need that level of protection, he said. "The state of the art for everyone is to have a portfolio of models," he explained. "In fact, I think most people don't know that the best model in the world's not Astra. The best model in the world's not Fable. The best model is literally a portfolio and we can prove it. You are always better routing between a few models than to do one singular model." That's what Fireworks does through Nexus and its API, alongside competitors like Together AI, Baseten, and DeepInfra. As a managed inference platform, Fireworks AI routes inference tasks to whichever model, frontier model subscription, or API is best suited to handle them. But the company is not just doing naive routing like an AI gateway. It's evaluating tasks as they come in and directing them to the optimal model. "We build custom routers," Ferguson explained. "Our auto model is continuously updating so that we actually go through and we grade the difficulty of the task and we see if there're affinities that the models have, like Kimi is slightly better at JavaScript than Python, things like this." The company's competitive edge, he contends, is its crack engineering team, which follows from its founders' work on PyTorch, a widely used open source machine learning library. "We're performance experts both on the training and inference side," he explained. "People I think don't understand how important, for example, numerics is. So when you use a model, it's always called a mixture of experts – an expert is a different machine. "And so you have all these different machines. It actually matters when you're training that you go back to precisely the right machine, because if you don't, the other machine will still answer the question, but it'll answer in a slightly different way. So we have to know how to build the topology to write back the data to the right space. We have to understand floating point precision [to handle very small values]. We have to be able to do all this where we're routing through a complex fabric through potentially more than one provider depending on what everything is. And so we're really systems

item.title: Okafor strike for Leeds ends Tottenham’s winning run
item.description: Leeds rode their luck to beat in-form Tottenham 1-0 on Saturday, benefiting from a controversial decision to allow Jayden Bogle to stay on the pitch after an ugly tackle on Mathys Tel. Substitute Noah Okafor was the match-winner, making an almost immediate impact after being introduced by Leeds boss Daniel Farke in the 77th minute. The home team started brightly and Spurs breathed a sigh of relief in the early minutes when VAR ruled that Mateus Fernandes had not handled the ball in the penalty area. As the first half wore on the visitors established themselves, though clear chances were at a premium. Leeds got the benefit of a contentious decision about 10 minutes before the break when Bogle caught Tel’s trailing ankle with his studs, leaving the Tottenham winger writhing on the ground in pain. After a lengthy VAR check no action was taken against Bogle, who was not even booked for the challenge, but Tel was forced off a few minutes later, hobbling off to be replaced by Dominic Solanke. Leeds had two big chances early in the second half as Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s header was blocked by Solanke before Nico Elvedi nodded wide on the follow-up. Calvert-Lewin then burst forward again but opted to pass to Ao Tanaka rather than shooting and the Japanese international skied his shot. Leeds were now on the front foot and Antonin Kinsky produced a wonderful stop after Sean Longstaff’s swivel and shot. But they got the goal their pressure deserved in the 79th minute. Harry Wilson, another substitute, controlled the ball and played it into the path of Okafor, who gave Kinsky no chance. Spurs came agonisingly close to an equaliser but goalkeeper James Trafford made a brilliant save from Jan Paul van Hecke’s header. The result ends Tottenham’s run of three straight league wins while it was the first victory in six games for Leeds, who climbed to eighth in the table. item.title: 2027: Collect campaign money, but vote your conscience, Makinde tells Nigerians
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Governor Seyi Makinde, has urged Nigerians to collect money offered to them by politicians during campaigns but vote according to their conscience. Makinde gave the advice during his presidential campaign flag-off in Bauchi, where he addressed supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections. He urged voters not to allow financial inducements to influence their electoral choices, insisting that accepting money from politicians should not translate into voting against their conscience. “When they bring money, it’s your money. Collect it, spend it, but vote your heart, and I know your heart is with us and with APM,” he told the gathering. The APM presidential candidate also called on Nigerians to support what he described as a national reset, arguing that economic hardship, insecurity and lack of inclusiveness in governance had made fundamental changes necessary. He questioned whether hunger among Nigerians should not prompt an economic reset, just as insecurity required a review of the country’s security architecture. Makinde further argued that the exclusion of many Nigerians from governance demanded a reset of the country’s socio-political environment. He said Nigerians dissatisfied with the state of affairs should embrace the proposed national reset, adding that the country needed a government capable of addressing public concerns with sincerity and transparency. He also appreciated Bauchi State Governor Bala Mohammed, whom he described as his national leader, the APM national chairman, and his wife for their support and encouragement. Akwa Ibom people, from where I came from, we have food in the market. “I don’t know, in Akwa Ibom, is there any person who took his money to the market and found out there’s no rice? “You didn’t answer me. item.description: Today’s developments centre on President Tinubu’s new infrastructure commitment during his South-South campaign, fresh World Bank figures on Nigeria’s external debt, and the release of long-stranded electricity equipment. In Africa, Sudan’s humanitarian agencies warn of a serious funding shortfall. Globally, AI-related stocks have recovered some of Thursday’s losses, although investors remain concerned about technology spending and regulation. 1. Nigeria 2027: Tinubu approves Ibom Deep Seaport project during South-South campaign ﻿ What happened: President Bola Tinubu announced approval of the proposed Ibom Deep Seaport at an APC rally in Uyo on Friday, 6 November, in response to a request from Akwa Ibom Governor Umo Eno. Eno described the project as critical to the state’s maritime economy and pledged to mobilise two million votes for Tinubu’s re-election. That is a political commitment, not an electoral forecast. The president is scheduled to attend another APC rally in Port Harcourt today. Why it matters: The long-delayed seaport could expand Nigeria’s cargo-handling capacity and support manufacturing, logistics and international trade if successfully financed and constructed. Strategic implications: The announcement links an important economic infrastructure proposal with the ongoing election campaign. Presidential approval does not yet establish an agreed financing structure or construction timetable. What to watch: Formal project approval documents, funding arrangements, implementation milestones and today’s Rivers State campaign activities. 2. Nigeria economy: World Bank puts total external debt at $145 billion The World Bank headquarters in Washington, DC, on April 13, 2022. The Spring meetings will take place virtually from April 22-25. Stefani Reynolds / AFP What happened: The World Bank’s International Debt Report 2026, released on 5 November and reported extensively on Friday, shows that Nigeria’s total external debt rose by 6.6% to $145.02 billion at the end of 2025. Nigerian Debt 2024 external debt $135.99bn 2025 external debt $145.02bn Public/guaranteed 43% Private 38% Short-term 19% The total includes approximately $62.4 billion in public and publicly guaranteed obligations, $54.5 billion in private nonguaranteed debt and $28.1 billion in short-term obligations. It must not be confused with government external debt alone. Why it matters: External debt servicing is consuming more export earnings, even as some indicators of debt sustainability have improved. Business and political implications: The figures warrant careful scrutiny alongside Tinubu’s revised $7.7 billion external borrowing proposal. Borrowing costs, project productivity and fiscal transparency will remain central to the government’s economic policy debate. Are mosquitoes not biting you?” He recalled Amaechi’s role as director-general of the presidential campaigns of former President Muhammadu Buhari. Wike said the then APC candidate failed to secure up to 15 percent of the votes in Rivers state in the 2015 and 2019 presidential elections. item.title: FG warns public against NTI admissions, cancels 2026 NCE, degree intake
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Ministry of Education has warned prospective students, parents and the general public against seeking admission into unauthorised National Certificate in Education (NCE) and degree programmes at the National Teachers’ Institute (NTI), Kaduna, following regulatory breaches involving admissions, accreditation and university affiliations. Consequently, all admissions into NTI’s NCE and degree programmes for the 2026 academic session have been cancelled, while the Institute has been directed to discontinue all university affiliations and degree-awarding arrangements, as it is not authorised to award NCE and university degrees. The ministry, in a statement by its Director, Press and Public Relations, Boriowo Folasade, emphasised that no further admissions into the affected programmes, whether full-time, part-time or through Distance Learning Studies (DLS), are permitted. Members of the public are therefore strongly advised not to apply, accept admission offers or make payments for such programmes. According to the statement, “The directive follows violations of the Ministerial Operational Guidelines issued on 12 September 2025. The Ministry clarifies that NCE admissions must comply with applicable Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) requirements and accreditation standards of the National Commission for Colleges of Education (NCCE).” “The National Universities Commission (NUC) is also to notify affected universities and ensure compliance with the directive on NTI’s discontinued degree-awarding arrangements,” the statement added. “To protect innocent students already enrolled, the NCCE will conduct comprehensive accreditation of existing NCE II–IV Distance Learning programmes and study centres across the six geopolitical zones. Eligible students may complete their programmes, subject to accreditation outcomes and regulatory requirements, “it further added. The ministry reiterated that NTI’s statutory mandate remains teacher training, retraining, in-service development and continuous professional development. This includes pedagogical capacity-building and the three-to-six-month Special Abridged Programme for serving teachers with non-education degrees to acquire the professional competencies required for registration with the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN), subject to applicable regulations. The ministry stressed that the intervention is intended to protect students, uphold academic standards and prevent further exposure of prospective applicants to unapproved programmes. It urged the public to verify programme accreditation and admission status through relevant regulatory authorities and official government channels before making enrolment or payment decisions. The post FG warns public against NTI admissions, cancels 2026 NCE, degree intake appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Makinde: Tinubu’s poor planning plunged millions of Nigerians into hardship
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has blamed the economic hardship facing millions of Nigerians on what he described as inadequate planning by the President Bola Tinubu-led administration. Makinde said major economic policy decisions introduced by the Federal Government were implemented without adequate plans and frameworks to cushion their effects on citizens, thereby worsening the economic difficulties faced by Nigerians. The APM presidential candidate spoke on Friday during a live interview on the Bauchi Radio Corporation (BRC), while in Bauchi State to flag off his 2027 presidential campaign. He argued that the immediate impact of the administration’s economic policies on Nigerians was a consequence of taking major decisions without adequate preparation and effective implementation strategies. Makinde stressed that economic reforms must be supported by proper planning and clear implementation frameworks to ensure that ordinary citizens do not bear the brunt of government policies. He said addressing the country’s economic challenges would require fundamental structural reforms and strong political will. The Oyo governor also highlighted the APM’s Reset Nigeria Agenda, which he said was designed to address the country’s challenges through a documented policy framework and the party’s manifesto. According to him, the agenda focuses on reforming critical sectors of the economy, promoting sustainable development and restoring true federalism that recognises and respects Nigeria’s diverse nationalities. item.title: Star Wars is experiencing a golden age of video games
item.description: After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games . With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences. It's become clear that future Star Wars games needn't be expensive endeavors full of familiar faces or concepts. Star Wars Zero Company and Galactic Racer 's restrained scope and confidence have been infectious, and, as it turns out, they're already recognized by all the parties involved as double-A success stories . Now this is podracing! (Image credit: Secret Mode) A Burnout-inspired Star Wars racer (created by a bunch of ex-Burnout devs) is a fantastic pitch if you know your video games, but looking at EA's recent and current direction, it's easy to see why it didn't happen under their reign. The original Burnout studio, Criterion, would have been an excellent candidate, but instead they were sent to work in the Battlefield mines. Still, someone was interested in the idea, and the end result is glorious. Fast and furious, Star Wars: Galactic Racer ignores recent racing game trends and bets big on arcade-y vibes, uncomplicated controls, and a high skill ceiling that challenges you with extremely high speeds, tight turns, and unexpected interruptions as other drivers try to ruin your day. The not-so-secret sauce, however, was its runs-based structure, which injects the flexibility and replay value of roguelite games into the more traditional arcade racing structure that older gamers are familiar with. (Image credit: EA) Fully confident in its central gameplay idea and devoid of modern live-service baggage, Fuse Games' debut title makes the most of the Star Wars setting within the restrictions of simply making a fun and engaging Star Wars racer. It's almost the same approach we felt in Zero Company, a turn-based tactical strategy-RPG that comes from the minds of another team of ex-triple-A developers. "Star Wars but XCOM" should've happened earlier, but we're glad it did this year, and, unsurprisingly, it's a banger. The correct read of their success should be obvious (and so far, it appears the powers that be are seeing it): Let seasoned and fresh developers cook games they're excited about. Big, medium, or small, players will react positively to experiences that really feel genuine and aren't brought down by tacked-on systems or monetization. item.title: Explainer: Who won 2023 presidential 2023 in Kaduna, Katsina – the 161,829 votes difference
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi – ABUJA Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, won Katsina State in the February 25, 2023 presidential election by only 6,762 votes over Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, according to results declared by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC. Read Also: * Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal * How Buhari promised me APC presidential ticket in 2022; I regret listening to him – Amaechi He also won neighbouring Kaduna State, where his lead was far wider. Katsina: a margin of 6,762 votes Atiku polled 489,045 votes in Katsina, against Tinubu’s 482,283. Out of 1,058,673 valid votes, that is a gap of about 0.64 of a percentage point. Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party, NNPP, came third with 69,386 votes. Peter Obi, who ran on the Labour Party, LP, ticket, had just 6,376 votes. Katsina had 3,516,719 registered voters. The 1,058,673 valid votes represent about 30 per cent of that figure. Kaduna: a lead of 155,067 votes Kaduna was not close. Atiku scored 554,360 votes to Tinubu’s 399,293, a lead of 155,067. Obi came third in Kaduna with 294,494 votes, and Kwankwaso was fourth with 92,969. The state had 4,335,208 registered voters, of whom 1,418,046 were accredited. INEC recorded 1,360,153 valid votes and 41,223 rejected votes, making 1,401,376 votes cast in total. Where the two states differ Obi’s vote shows the sharpest contrast. He polled 294,494 votes in Kaduna. But he got only 6,376 in Katsina, where he finished fourth behind Kwankwaso. Across both states, Atiku polled 1,043,405 votes and Tinubu 881,576, giving Atiku a combined lead of 161,829. Obi had 300,870 votes and Kwankwaso 162,355. Nearly all of Atiku’s combined lead came from Kaduna. Katsina added only 6,762 votes to it. item.title: Kalu urges Igbo leaders to unite, engage in Nigerian politics
item.description: Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, has urged Igbo elders, leaders and stakeholders to unite and take a more active role in Nigeria’s politics, warning that disunity and political apathy have weakened the South-East’s influence in national affairs. The call was contained in a statement issued on Saturday by his Chief Press Secretary, Levinus Nwabughiogu. Kalu also called for a change of mindset among Igbo people, particularly those who have traditionally focused on developing their communities while keeping away from national politics. He made the call on Friday at the South-East Stakeholders’ Convergence, also known as the South-East Elders and Stakeholders Meeting, held at the Imo State Government House, Owerri. The meeting, convened to discuss unity, peace and development in Igbo land, was chaired by a former Military Governor of Imo State and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Senator Ike Nwachukwu. Kalu, who represents Bende Federal Constituency of Abia State, said unity was essential to the political relevance and development of the South-East, stressing that the region could achieve more if its leaders and people worked towards common goals. “Unity is strength. We will achieve more when we are united. The need for unity cannot be overemphasised. Peace leads to the development of communities,” he said. Commending the elders and stakeholders for attending the meeting despite their individual engagements, the Deputy Speaker described their gathering as an expression of patriotism and commitment to the progress of Igbo land. He said their example would encourage younger generations to sustain the quest for unity and development, likening leadership to a relay race in which older generations hand over the baton to their successors. Kalu, however, warned that the Igbo people risked losing their heritage and political direction if they continued to operate in isolation. On the region’s political influence, he said the numerical strength of the Igbo was not adequately reflected in the political fortunes of the five South-East states, partly because many people from the region lived in other parts of the country. He argued that a common political agenda would enable the Igbo to consolidate their strength and make their voices more influential in national decision-making. “The number of votes of Ndi Igbo is not what we are getting across the five states because we are scattered around the country. If we take a position now and say, Igbo, this is our agenda, this is what we want to do, I can assure you, the whole of Nigeria will feel our impact,” he said. The Deputy Speaker also urged the people to abandon what he described as the post-civil war mindset of avoiding national politics and concentrating solely on developing their communities. item.title: The Bantu expansion changed Africa. Scientists are still tracing how.
item.description: It’s not easy to extract iron from its ore. But the peoples of the ancient city of Great Zimbabwe—the capital of a thriving kingdom in southern Africa between 1000 to 1700 AD—were masters. At sites near the city’s stone ruins, clusters of iron-smelting furnaces survive today as mounds of rubble. At Mashava, a village 25 miles northwest, fragments bear fingermarks of those who long ago smoothed the structures’ clay interiors. Some of the furnaces were nearly an adult’s arm span in width, with walls thick and strong to contain the heat of more than 2,100° Fahrenheit needed to smelt iron. Unlike other furnaces that required workers to force air into them with bellows, these were designed to suck air in, then out through a chimney, no human labor required. This would have made it significantly easier to produce the iron, which was fashioned into hoes, axes, and arrowheads. Read full article Comments

It was a single panel comic strip filled with non-sequitur, surreal jokes mostly aimed at adults instead of children, which was unusual for newspaper comics at the time. Also unusual was the fact that, unlike most daily comic strips, The Far Side had no recurring characters. Peanuts has its gang of kids and Garfield has its cast of humans and animals, but every panel of The Far Side introduces new characters and scenarios all aimed at delivering one single joke.
