item.title: Dimorphos in sight: Europe's Hera probe gets its 1st look at battered space rock (photo)
item.description: null Europe's Hera planetary defense spacecraft is closing in on the binary asteroid system targeted by NASA's DART deflection test, and can now tell the two rocky bodies apart. Hera is nearing the end of its voyage to the Didymos asteroid system, having launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket in October 2024. The spacecraft snapped the image of Didymos and the smaller Dimorphos on Oct. 18 from a distance of 795 miles (1280 kilometers) from the pair, which are currently about 122 million miles (197 million km) from Earth. "With this image, the smaller Dimorphos asteroid becomes visible for the first time," Michael Kueppers, Hera project scientist at the European Space Agency (ESA), said in a statement . "Before this acquisition, the spacecraft was still resolving the Didymos system as a single dot. But now, even though Dimorphos is made up of only around one pixel in this initial image, it is clearly well separated from its parent body." The Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) smashed into Dimorphos in September 2022, changing the asteroid's orbit in a pioneering planetary defense demonstration. Hera's job is to survey the damage and refine our understanding of the impact, as well as the asteroids themselves. Hera performed braking maneuvers earlier in October to slow its approach and put it on course to rendezvous with the binary system. The spacecraft is designed to make follow-up observations of the asteroids using 12 payloads, providing new insights that will prove valuable for planetary defense efforts. The mission also carries a pair of cubesats for a closer look and eventual landing on the 495-foot-wide (151 meters) Dimorphos. A series of images captured by the DART spacecraft as it sped to impact the asteroid Dimorphos on Sept. 26, 2022. (Image credit: NASA/JHUAPL) For now, Hera is continuing its approach and preparing for arrival, with a big reveal expected to occur later this month. "Our views will grow much sharper as Hera comes closer," said ESA's mission manager Ian Carnelli. "We will unveil the first detailed images of Dimorphos — the first object in the solar system to have had its orbit measurably shifted by human action — on 25 November."

item.title: Ejiro Amos Tafiri Unveils REVERIE, Its Spring/Summer 2027 Collection, Celebrating Reinvention in African Luxury
item.description: Ejiro Amos Tafiri , a Pan-African luxury fashion house founded in Lagos in 2010, has unveiled REVERIE, its Spring/Summer 2027 (SS27) collection, at an exclusive private showcase in Lagos on Sunday, October 25, 2026, held alongside Lagos Fashion Week. The showcase brought together distinguished guests, fashion industry leaders, patrons and representatives of the British Council Nigeria, including chef and media personality Hilda Baci, for a presentation of the house’s latest collection. REVERIE explores renewal and reinvention through contemporary African luxury. Bringing together expressive silhouettes, intricate craftsmanship and a refined colour palette, the collection presents a visual statement that celebrates the evolving language of African fashion. Through considered design and craftsmanship, REVERIE reflects the house’s continued exploration of contemporary African aesthetics, presenting pieces that balance creative expression with the distinctive design sensibility for which Ejiro Amos Tafiri is known. Founded by designer Ejiro Amos Tafiri, known for her signature Drapes, the fashion house has spent 16 years developing a distinctive identity within the luxury fashion landscape. Its design language is characterized by expressive drapery, fluid tailoring and the thoughtful use of indigenous textiles, bringing African craftsmanship into contemporary fashion. The Lagos unveiling followed the third edition of Fashioning a Legacy: Leaving a Mark in Time, held on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at the British Council in Ikoyi, Lagos. The conference brought together designers, stylists, retail professionals and emerging creatives to discuss building sustainable careers and creating lasting impact within the fashion industry. Together, the events reflect Ejiro Amos Tafiri’s continued engagement with the broader creative ecosystem, connecting fashion, education, craftsmanship and the development of emerging talent. The REVERIE presentation forms part of the house’s 16-year milestone and will be followed by an exclusive showcase in Abuja on November 21, 2026. The forthcoming event will bring together members of the diplomatic community, government officials, fashion patrons and invited guests for a further presentation of the house’s work. As Ejiro Amos Tafiri looks towards its next chapter, REVERIE embodies an ongoing exploration of renewal and reinvention, reinforcing the house’s commitment to advancing contemporary African luxury through expressive design and intricate craftsmanship. item.title: Hubble Telescope sees cosmic 'cat's tail' that could wrap around Earth and the sun 500 times
item.description: null Using the Hubble Space Telescope, astronomers have investigated a cosmic cat's tail, finding it likely formed after two Pluto-sized bodies smashed together. The feature, nicknamed the Cat's Tail, extends out from the debris disk known as Beta Pictoris which is located in a planetary system located 63 light-years away. This tail would put that of the average tabby to shame: It's so long that it could curl around the sun-Earth system about 500 times. That's about as long as 200 trillion house cats. The major difference between our solar system and the planetary system that hosts the Cat's Tail is the latter's relative youth. While our solar system is around 4.6 billion years old , Beta Pictoris is a cosmic kitten no more than a few million years old. That means it is still host to collisions between planetary bodies similar to the ones that rocked the solar system during its infancy. The team behind this research gained new insights into the Cat's Tail using 14 years of observations. This allowed them to solve the long-standing mystery of the violent conditions under which it formed. "The Cat's Tail is thought to be the aftermath of a collision between large bodies — think something like Pluto ," team leader Arin Avsar of the University of Arizona said in a statement. "Oddly, this feature had previously only been seen with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), which detects infrared light, but remained invisible at shorter wavelengths, which has puzzled the community for a while." Cosmic cat tail is also pleasingly fluffy Comparing Beta Pictoris and our solar system, one thing rapidly becomes apparent: our cosmic neighborhood is relatively well-ordered. The planets orbit the sun with most space rocks neatly delegated into bands: the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter , and the Kuiper belt out beyond the orbit of Neptune. However, this is a stark contrast to the solar system's violent and chaotic youth. Back then, the solar system was host to an infant star surrounded by a swirling disk of gas and dust in which collisions between bodies called planetesimals — the building blocks of planets — were commonplace. Astronomers can't look back to the solar system's infancy, so to learn more about how our cosmic backyard took shape, they study nearby young planetary systems. Systems like Beta Pictoris. That doesn't mean it has been quick to divulge its secrets, though. "We think the Cat's Tail has eluded our observations in visible light until now because of what it's made of," Avsar explained. "It consists almost entirely of what we call organic refractory material, which is heavily carbon-based. These long chains of carbon atoms absorb visible light, so they're quite black." This new study revealed that the feline feature is cat-like in more ways than just its shape. It's also pleasingly fluffy, Hubble observations suggest. item.title: Pan-African School Games 2026: Celebrating Young Talent, School Pride and New Opportunities
item.description: The Pan-African School Games 2026 brought together young athletes from schools across Lagos for three days of swimming, athletics and football, celebrating sporting talent, school pride and the opportunities that organized competition can create for children and young people. Held at James Hope College, Lekki, from 16 to 18 October, the second edition of the Games featured the U-11, U-13 and U-15 categories. Students competed for individual honours and school points while gaining valuable experience in a structured, multi-sport environment. The competition also welcomed sporting stakeholders and scouts, reinforcing the wider ambition of the Pan-African School Games: to give young athletes a platform where their abilities can be demonstrated, recognized and developed. Building on the Inaugural Games The second edition of the Pan-African School Games built on the foundation established by the inaugural Games in 2025, continuing the vision of creating meaningful sporting opportunities for young athletes. The 2026 edition welcomed schools and student-athletes for three days of swimming, athletics and football, providing a platform for competition, talent development and school pride. Beyond the sporting results, the Games continued to advance a broader ambition: to connect schools, athletes, sporting stakeholders and educational institutions while creating opportunities for young people to develop their abilities and explore future pathways through sport. Day One: Swimming Opens the Games Swimming opened the competition, bringing young swimmers together for races across the U-11, U-13 and U-15 categories. The opening day set the pace for the Games as athletes took to the pool to test their abilities, pursue strong performances and earn points for their schools. The races highlighted the preparation, discipline and technique required to compete, while providing young swimmers with valuable experience in a formal sporting environment. For many of the students, the opportunity to compete alongside athletes from other schools added to the significance of the experience. Each race contributed to the overall competition, with schools beginning their campaigns for medals and category honours. Day Two: Athletics Puts Young Athletes to the Test Athletics took centre stage on the second day, with track and field events testing the speed, strength, coordination and technique of the young competitors. Athletes competed in running, jumping and throwing events, earning points for their schools as the standings developed. Each discipline presented a different challenge, giving students opportunities to demonstrate their abilities and compete for individual and team honours. The athletics programme added another dimension to the Games, highlighting the variety of talent within the participating schools and the value of giving young athletes opportunities to develop through competition. item.title: The 2027 'eclipse of the century' will plunge real Star Wars filming locations into darkness
item.description: null On Aug. 2, 2027, the moon's shadow will sweep across some of the most iconic filming locations from Star Wars, plunging them into darkness during what's being called the " eclipse of the century" . The path of the 2027 total solar eclipse will cross southern Tunisia, where several locations were used to bring the fictional desert planet Tatooine to life. From the dunes of Mos Espa to the rocky Jundland Wastes, Star Wars fans will have the rare opportunity to experience totality at the very places where their favorite scenes were filmed But not every famous filming location will experience totality, so choosing where to watch will be crucial. Here are four locations that fall directly in the moon's shadow. All times, totality durations and historical cloud cover data come from Time and Date . 1. Eriguet dunes (Mos Espa) Built for Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace , the Mos Espa film set in the Tunisian desert. (Image credit: Chiara Salvadori via Getty Images) Location: south of Chott el-Gharsa, Tozeur Governorate, southwest Tunisia Start of totality and duration: 10:06 a.m. CET; 2 minutes, 9 seconds Chance of clouds: 2% With a massive budget and three prequels to make, Lucasfilm built a new film set that would double as the Mos Espa spaceport on Tatooine for The Phantom Menace and Attack of the Clones . This is where Qui-Gon Jinn, Obi-Wan Kenobi, Jar Jar Binks and Padme get stranded, where they meet Anakin Skywalker and where the podrace takes place. Now abandoned , it's in the middle of nowhere, between two huge salt lakes and subject to the intense heat and moving Eriguet dunes — but it is firmly within the path of totality. Nearby are two other shooting locations — the Ong Jemel outcrop , where Darth Maul arrives on the scene, and Yardang , where Qui-Gon and Darth Maul battle — the first-ever lightsaber duel filmed on location. 2. Maguer Gorge (Jundland Wastes) Tourists enjoy sunset at Onk Jemal, the desert location of "Star Wars" movies. (Image credit: Maremagnum via Getty Images) Location: Jebel Sidi Bouhlel canyon, Dghoumès National Park, Tozeur, southwest Tunisia Start of totality and duration: 10:06 a.m. CET; 3 minutes, 37 seconds Chance of clouds: 1% Often called "Star Wars Canyon" by fans and crew, Maguer Gorge in Jebel Sidi Bouhlel doubled as the Jundland Wastes of Tatooine in Star Wars: Episode IV — A New Hope . It's where Luke Skywalker is attacked by Tusken Raiders, where Obi-Wan Kenobi first appears and where Luke and Obi-Wan discover the slaughtered Jawas. The canyon also provided the distant view of Mos Eisley — the famous "wretched hive of scum and villainy." On Aug. 2, 2027, you'll likely be pointing your macrobinoculars at the eclipsed sun rather than Tusken Raiders. Steven Spielberg later filmed here for Raiders of the Lost Ark , including the scene in which Indiana Jones threatens to destroy the Ark with a bazooka. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 3, 1957: Laika the dog launches with Sputnik 2
item.description: null On Nov. 3, 1957, a Soviet space dog named Laika became the first animal to orbit Earth. Laika was a 3-year-old stray husky-spitz mix from the streets of Moscow, and she was recruited by the Soviet space program for her small size and calm temperament. Unfortunately for Laika, this mission was a one-way trip . The Soviets didn't design a way to bring her back down to Earth. With only 7 days worth of oxygen and a little bit of food on board, Laika launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan with a Russian Sputnik rocket. This was the same kind of rocket used to launch the first Sputnik satellite. Laika was alive when she reached orbit, but she died shortly afterward because the spacecraft's heat shield had broken off. Laika overheated before she had the chance to die of starvation of oxygen deprivation. Laika, the first Soviet space dog to enter Earth orbit, is seen in a training capsule prior to her launch. (Image credit: Roscosmos) Why it mattered Laika has remained one of space history's most beloved and tragic figures. People around the world have dogs as pets who they love as members of their own families. And even nearly 70 years after this flight, it is so heartbreaking to think of Laika on that frightening journey from which she never returned. Laika was one of many different animals that were used in early spaceflight testing. Both the U.S. and Russia launched a number of primates on flights testing early flight technology. Sadly, like Laika, many of these brave creatures did not make it back. Unbelievably, though, some did survive the journey. For example, the chimpanzee named Ham and nicknamed the "astrochimp" survived a 1961 test flight to space. Though, the team behind that flight was so unsure of how it would go that Ham didn't get his name until after it was found that he'd survived his return. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Robot cube explores the International Space Station | Space photo of the day for Nov. 3, 2026
item.description: null An Astrobee, a tiny robot cube, is zipping around the International Space Station helping out the astronauts on board. (Image credit: NASA/Jessica Watkins) A tiny robot cube is zipping around the International Space Station, trying to help astronauts with the endless challenging tasks onboard. What is it? Reminiscent of Rocky rolling around the lab helping out Dr. Ryland Grace in Project Hail Mary, the Astrobee robot is a helpful assistant for astronauts aboard the space station . A metal cube about the size of a toaster, the Astrobees are free-flying robotic assistants that NASA developed to help out astronauts. The first two Astrobee robots (named Bumble and Honey) were sent to the station in 2019. The third Astrobee robot, named Queen, joined later that year, and 7 years later, the program is still going strong. So what can a free-floating cube help with? The robots are designed to assist the astronauts onboard with testing new technologies in microgravity and helping mission team members back on Earth to better observe inside the station. The little robot cubes can even help astronauts with everyday chores in space. In this image , snapped by NASA astronaut and Crew-13 commander Jessica Watkins, we can see one of the Astrobee robots helping out in the station's Kibo laboratory. Why is it incredible? The idea of a robot assistant helping out with chores and technology development aboard an orbiting space laboratory sounds positively science fiction. While Astrobee is certainly not the first robot in space or aboard the space station, its compact shape and ability to fly autonomously gives it a unique quality. It really looks like a companion aboard the space station. While the robotic space helpers of today might be cute little cubes, the success of the Astrobee program begs the question of how robots in space might continue to evolve. Will astronauts on the moon have robotic companions autonomously exploring and helping out? What will they look like?

Organized by Afreximbank in collaboration with the African Union and the AfCFTA Secretariat, Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX WKND) is Africa’s premier event celebrating the continent’s creative and cultural industries. Under the overarching theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World: From FESTAC ’77 to CANEX ’27,” this year’s gathering will connect thousands of creative entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers, and cultural icons from across Global Africa and the diaspora. Spotlighting Francophone Luxury & Made-in-Africa Fashion As part of this landmark event, Afrique Femme is hosting a dedicated Exhibition Pavilion designed to bridge Francophone and Anglophone creative ecosystems. The pavilion will feature curated showcases, pop-ups, and private sales from leading West and Central African designers. Attendees will experience exclusive collections from celebrated brands including Makeda by AYA Konan ,, KUMI , KWELAKU , and Galipette Atelier , highlighting the richness, craftsmanship, and global potential of Francophone fashion. The African Woman 2.0 VIP Networking Brunch A core highlight of the week will take place on Saturday, November 7, 2026 , with the African Woman 2.0 VIP Networking Brunch . Bringing together 200 to 250 influential women leaders, policymakers, innovators, and international dignitaries, the high-level gathering will feature keynote addresses, strategic panels, and structured B2B networking aimed at fostering female leadership and economic empowerment across the continent. “We are thrilled to bring the African Woman 2.0 platform to Lagos alongside CANEX WKND 2026,” said Aïssata Sidibé N’DIA , Managing Director of RED Côte d’Ivoire / Afrique Femme. “This partnership offers an extraordinary opportunity to celebrate the ingenuity of African creative entrepreneurs, showcase Francophone fashion excellence on a global stage, and build lasting cross-border trade and investment synergies across Africa.” Event & Registration Details Dates: November 5–8, 2026 Venue: Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture & Creative Arts (National Theatre), Lagos, Nigeria Registration: Delegate attendance at CANEX WKND 2026 is 100% free , but pre-registration is mandatory. item.title: African Philanthropy Leaders Call for Bolder, Locally Led Giving at the 2026 APF Conference in Cape Town
item.description: CAPE TOWN, South Africa: African Philanthropy Forum (APF) closed its 2026 Conference in Cape Town on 27 October with a message that ran through nearly every session: Africa’s challenges are connected, so African giving has to be connected too. Held from 25 to 27 October under the theme Bridge the Divide; Reimagine the Future , the conference brought together philanthropists, funders, business leaders, creatives, and technologists to ask how African capital can be mobilized, how partnerships can be strengthened, and how African-led solutions can be backed with more trust and flexibility. Centered on Africa, the program also looked outward, drawing on solutions from across the Global South and asking how African philanthropy can bridge the divide. The conference opened on Sunday evening with a reception at Cape Point Vineyards, where Executive Director Mosun Layode welcomed delegates, members and acknowledged APF Board members, including Chair Gbenga Oyebode , Wale Adeosun , and Nyimpini Mabunda . Former Board Member Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa urged guests to look past the continent’s challenges and toward its potential and to use the days ahead to turn conversations into partnerships. It was an evening of connection before two days of ideas at the Norval Foundation. Reimagining the Future Monday, 26 October, began with a call to build bridges across regions, languages, and funding silos. Mosun Layode and Gbenga Oyebode officially opened and welcomed all delegates to the conference. Dr. Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka , former Vice President of South Africa, spoke of education as a sacred right of every African child and of bringing young people into decision-making. In the first keynote, Gary Lubner, Founder of the This Day Foundation, described giving away 95 percent of his wealth during his lifetime and said it was easier and more joyful than holding it for heirs. Old money thinking, he argued, is a major barrier to giving, and generosity includes time and effort as well as cash. The numbers framed the challenge. Delegates heard that Africa needs about $1.3 trillion in financing each year, while philanthropy contributes $5 billion to $6 billion. The task is to use that small pool to unlock far larger sources, such as pension funds and fixed-income assets, so money reaches businesses that create jobs. In an afternoon keynote moderated by Marlene Ogawa of Synergos, Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa , South Africa CEO of Naspers, and Gareth Ackerman, Non-Executive Director at Pick n Pay, kept things practical: back women entrepreneurs without taking equity, start with your own family and community, use local distributors, and make it easier to travel between African countries. One retraining program they discussed moved 7,200 of 8,000 university graduates into tech jobs. The difference between charity and philanthropy, they said, is helping people help themselves. The day also asked hard questions about who belongs. A panel on migration, moderated by Dr Ndidi Okonkw

item.title: AI & Equity: The Big Conversations at Goalkeepers Dakar 2026
item.description: The Goalkeepers 2026 Event in Dakar brought together innovators, global leaders and experts on how AI can be further leveraged by Africans for an equitable future On October 29, 2026, Africans gathered in Dakar, Senegal, to discuss the continent’s relationship with the world’s fastest-growing technology: artificial intelligence (AI). This event was part of the Goalkeepers 2026 series and was themed “Make This Matter: Equitable AI and the Future of African Youth .” It brought together professionals and innovators who focused on how Africa can adopt AI to fill gaps and ensure equitable access across various sectors . Africans are leveraging AI for business, education and more, but as AI continues to develop and expand rapidly, it is crucial for us to use it on a bigger scale, ensuring collective development and an equitable future for all. This makes the Goalkeepers 2026 event in Dakar particularly significant. Nigerian influencer, Saskay, at Goalkeepers Dakar 2026 The event included several activities, including performances from the legendary Youssou N’Dour , a Qui veut changer le monden session where people pitched their ideas, conversations about AI and equity and more. Here are some of the major talking points at the event: AI and Existing Solutions The event was graciously hosted in English and French by Fatou Jupiter Toure , who opened by sharing a powerful African message: “It is not about what you can do. It is about what we can do for each other.” Despite the diverse cultures and beliefs that exist on the continent, Africans have remained held by the belief of “I am because you are.” This is why, despite AI’s fast growth, Africans are coming together to examine how much it concerns them, how it can be properly leveraged and what dangers and challenges lie ahead. Fatou Jupiter Toure hosting the Goalkeepers 2026 event in Dakar Nevertheless, Africans have done a great deal of work with AI. Innovators have used AI tools to provide solutions in their local communities. Vyonne Njeri shared how she got into healthcare and how AI has been greatly helping in the community she serves. In the Goalkeepers 2026 Report , Vyonne said she got into healthcare during a visit to see her uncle, a priest in a small, East Kenyan town called Modogashe. She highlighted that even though AI greatly supports her work, she remains the clinical officer. She explained that “AI is not perfect. It must not take over clinical work. But it can help us share across accessible healthcare. It can help discover what could have been missed early. We still need people to be trained, but AI tools can greatly support us.” Like Vyonne, Mamadou Ly also shared why and how AI can aid learning, especially in local languages. He said, “Education is not just about reading and writing. It is also an act of dignity.” Mamadou Ly at Goalkeepers Dakar 2026. item.title: LagosFashionWeek2026: Personal Style Is Alive and Well – Just Ask Ifeoma Odogwu
item.description: From runway shows to intimate presentations and the week’s most stylish gatherings, the fashion editor and creative consultant made a case for directional dressing with oodles of personality. Ifeoma Odogwu , better known as Hyperfashun , is easily one of the best dressed women in Lagos, and arguably on the continent and per usual her Lagos Fashion Week style is peerless. A familiar face in Nigeria’s fashion industry, the former Genevieve Magazine fashion editor, stylist to stars such as Toke Makinwa and more, the creative consultant has spent years working with designers, discovering emerging talent and helping shape the visual language of Nigerian fashion. So, naturally, when Lagos Fashion Week comes around, we’re just as interested in what she’s wearing as we are in what she’s watching. From the bustling Lagos Fashion Week tents at Federal Palace Hotel to a packed calendar of offsite presentations and fashion events across the city, Odogwu embraced the occasion with a wardrobe that made getting dressed part of the experience. At the tents, she joined the fashion crowd for presentations by Y’Wande , NYA The Label , E.S.O by Liman and FIA Factory , taking in some of the exciting design talent shaping the season. But as anyone familiar with Lagos Fashion Week knows, the shows have evolved. Some of the week’s most interesting moments happen elsewhere, and Odogwu’s itinerary reflected just how much the city’s fashion calendar has expanded. She made the rounds at presentations by Jewel Jemila , The Ladymaker, Rendoll, Kilentar, Onalaja and Orange Culture , and made time for the social side of fashion week, too, including the Made By Us pop-up at Melrose Loft and Tiffany Amber’s Breakfast Club. What makes Odogwu particularly interesting to watch is the perspective she brings to personal style. As someone whose career has been built around fashion imagery, designers and creative expression, her wardrobe offers another way of engaging with the industry she’s helped champion. Ifeoma has a certain clarity in her style and an unmatched point of view, something that’s often lacking in the sameness of our Instagram-driven world. Her style reminds us that what makes personal style compelling is individuality, curiosity and a willingness to have fun with fashion. item.title: How the New Tax Stamp Could Show Up in Everyday Life
item.description: We’ve all been there: planning a weekend dinner with friends, throwing a birthday bash, or just kicking back at home with a few favourite treats. Drinks and refreshments are basically a staple of these moments. But have you ever stopped to think about how behind-the-scenes government policies end up changing the price tags on those items? With the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) rolling out its new excise stamp policy in January 2026, that question is at the forefront, especially for brands that make things like alcohol, tobacco, and sugar-sweetened beverages. Honestly, nobody’s really stressing over the policy itself. What people care about is the ripple effect: how companies handle the new regulation and whether those adjustments will make our favourite items more expensive on the shelf. When Business Meets Your Wallet Behind every product is a mountain of decisions from packaging and distribution to compliance and production. Most of the time, we never see this happening, but it plays a huge role in how items are priced. When new regulations bring extra costs, companies find themselves at a crossroads. Some choose to absorb the blow internally to keep customers happy, while others might tweak their prices. It really comes down to the specific brand, the market, and how heavy the financial lift is. For everyday shoppers, that’s usually the moment a boring policy talk suddenly feels very real. What Does This Mean for How We Spend ? The change probably won’t hit overnight, and it might not even be dramatic. But over time, small shifts in everyday prices can change how we shop. You might find yourself comparing brands a bit more closely, hunting for promos and discounts, or rethinking how much cash you drop on certain treats. Brands, meanwhile, are caught in a tricky balancing act: keeping loyal customers without going broke on rising operating costs. Just keep in mind: a new tax stamp doesn’t automatically mean prices are shooting up. It all depends on how companies adapt and whether those extra costs trickle down to us. The Bigger Picture At the end of the day, this is really about finding a middle ground. The government wants solid systems to collect taxes, while businesses need a framework that lets them stay afloat and grow. But come to think of it, the authorities are already equipped with internal tracking solutions, such as electronic invoicing from FIRS alongside the Customs Service’s B’Odogwu digital excise register, rendering physical paper tags largely redundant. Striking that balance matters because business decisions don’t just stay on a spreadsheet. They shape the things we buy, the choices we make, and how we manage our money. Right now, it’s still a bit early to tell what the full impact on consumers will be. But staying clued in on what’s driving the market makes it a whole lot easier to navigate the changes coming our way. Madam-carer, just let me be,” I grunted, picking up pebbles and tossing them back into the water. “No, seriously, I care about you. You left home claiming to go to your Alternative Therapist, yet look at you sitting by the beach playing with sand like a kindergartener,” Lantana said. “Lantana, please, do you mind? I really need my space right now.” “Abeg shift joor! Aunty lone-ranger. Every time you need your space, you need your space; you no dey tire of yourself?” “No, ma. I am still my best company.” “Very boring. How a human being can stay alone and claim that they are having fun by themself baffles me.” Lantana sits beside me and nudges closer. I side-eye her and shift aside. She moves closer. I sidle away; she comes closer and drapes her right leg across mine with a twinkle in her eyes. “Babe, free me na. I came here to breathe.” I begged. “You came here to breathe? Egbami, you been dey suffocate before? You left home to go to Iwona’s for therapy, so how did you now end up at the beach? “She say she get another customer.” I picked up a smooth pebble and a coral and lay back on the sand. “I no understand. She get another customer bi bawo? Didn’t you book this slot?” “I did.” “So, which kain talk be that?” Lantana was bristling already. “I was running late and sent her a message.” “You were running late? You ran from your house to here across three postcodes? With which strength abi you wan kpai?” Lantana looked worried. “Gaskiya, Lantana, you no get sense. Run as in how na? Shey today na Parkrun ni? I say I come late.” “Aha! That is what you should say na, auntie. You know you runners, once you say run, we take it literally.” “So, I go run the 22 miles because I want to prove what?” I glared at her. “Ah, a le so! We never can tell with weirdos like you.” She shot me a sly grin. “Lantana, I can’t deal right now. Just free me; let me breathe.” “So you came late? How many minutes late?” “26 minutes.” “Haba, that is so unlike you. What happened?” “I tried to catch the 3:15 bus but missed it. Then walked 15 minutes to the next bus stop, and the bus was delayed for 10 minutes. I decided to walk to the next one so I could catch a direct bus to her place, but that bus stop was closed. I went to the next one.” “Johnny Walka. Why didn’t you simply take a cab? See as you punish yourself on top £20.” “I no bi God na. I no see say na so e go bẹ.” I stood up, stretched and began walking into the waters. “Babe, you wan jump inside water? No koba mẹ o,” she screeched. “Olódò ni e. Jump say wetin happen? Say she save money wey I for pay the therapist?” “Wow, that is awesome. Look how you reframed it already. item.title: Who Checks on the Person Everyone Calls?
item.description: At 11:47 p.m., the family WhatsApp group suddenly comes alive. “Good evening, fam. Please, we have an emergency.” Before the second message arrives, everyone already knows who will be tagged. The eldest daughter who always knows what to do. The brother with the most stable job. The aunty abroad. The uncle in Lagos who “knows somebody.” The cousin with a car. The friend who always picks up, even at an unreasonable hour. In many Nigerian families, care has a name and a phone number. It belongs to the person who pays the unexpected bill, makes the difficult call, accompanies someone to the hospital, settles the family disagreement, or says, “Don’t worry, I’ll handle it.” We call them strong. Responsible. Dependable. We praise their shoulders without asking if they hurt. This is the human question at the heart of AXA Mansard’ s Culture of Care campaign: “ Who cares for the person everyone calls”? The Person Who Always Finds a Way Every family, friendship circle and workplace has one. Sometimes, she is the firstborn daughter who became a second mother long before she was ready. She remembers birthdays, school fees, hospital appointments, and the details everyone else forgets. Sometimes, he is the brother whose first good job quietly turned him into the family’s emergency fund and dependable source. His salary has not grown significantly, but the number of people depending on it has. Other times, it is the mom who serves everyone’s food before sitting down to eat. The father who never admits that he is worried. The friend who listens to everyone’s problems but rarely talks about her own. The colleague who carries the team whenever someone falls behind. These people are often so good at caring that we stop seeing the effort involved. We see the transfer alert, but not the personal plan they postponed. We see the paid bills, but not the hours spent calling doctors, arranging transport, and sitting beside a bed. We see the calm voice saying, “Everything will be fine,” but not the fear or uncertainty behind it. That person everyone calls may also be tired. They may worry about money, struggle with their health, or quietly wonder who would come through for them if they could no longer carry everyone else. Care Has More Than One Currency In Nigeria, many conversations about family responsibility often begin and end with money. Who paid the school fees? Who sent money home? Who handled the rent? Who covered the medical emergency? These questions matter, especially as the cost of living continues to stretch households. But money is only one currency of care. Care can also be time ! The sitting in traffic to pick up someone else’s child; the night spent at the hospital bedside; the regular reminder to an elderly parent to remember their medication. Or listening to the same worry repeatedly because the person telling you has nowhere else to take it. Care can be access ! Advice. Attention. Prayer. Food. Transport. Encouragement. A job referral. item.title: Meet Mo Odukoya: Pastor Jimmy Introduces His Wife to The Fountain of Life Church
item.description: Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and Pastor Mo Odukoya pose together following their formal church introduction If you’re a member of The Fountain of Life Church and you were at yesterday’s service, we’re a little jealous. What do you mean you got to witness Pastor Jimmy Odukoya introduce his wife, Mo Jasmine Daniel , to the congregation in person? Yes, right there at the church’s headquarters in Ilupeju, Lagos, the senior pastor had a special person to introduce, and he made sure everyone knew exactly who she was. As she joined him at the altar, he introduced her as Pastor Mo Odukoya , the church’s new first lady, and the congregation welcomed the couple with cheers and applause. Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and his wife, Mo Jasmine Daniel, holding hands during their official introduction at The Fountain of Life Church But before that introduction, Pastor Jimmy had a little story to tell. He spoke about how he had been navigating life alone since becoming the church’s senior pastor, and how he had been searching for someone to share the journey with. He invited Mo to join him, and the two walked up to the altar together, marking the moment with a warm reception from the congregation. Pastor Jimmy Odukoya introduces his wife, Mo Jasmine Daniel, on stage at The Fountain of Life Church in Ilupeju, Lagos For those who know Pastor Jimmy beyond the pulpit, there’s quite a bit to his story. He took over as senior pastor of The Fountain of Life Church in 2023, following the passing of his father, the late Pastor Taiwo Odukoya , who co-founded the ministry with his wife, Pastor Bimbo Odukoya . He is also an actor and musician, and film audiences may recognise him as Oba Ade in the 2022 historical film The Woman King, where he starred alongside Viola Davis . Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and Mo Jasmine Daniel after announcing their marriage to the congregation And now, there’s a new chapter to this story with Mo. Introduced to the congregation as Pastor Mo Odukoya, she is the daughter of Reverend Theophilus and Bolaji Daniel . She also took a moment to address the church, expressing her pleasure and honour at joining the ministry family. The couple also made sure their outfits were in sync for the occasion. Pastor Jimmy wore a structured burnt-orange native outfit with dark detailing on the cuffs and a matching necklace, while Pastor Mo chose a long-sleeved, floor-length dress in orange and copper patterns, finished with a matching clutch and accessories. item.title: You Should Treat Yourself to a Memorable Destination Birthday in 2027 If You Were Born Between 1977 and 1987
item.description: Christmas is now around the corner, and many of us will already be discussing plans for 2027. Some people will be thinking about new jobs, planning weddings or promising themselves they will finally start exercising next year. Then there are the 1977 and 1987 babies for whom 2027 won’t simply be another year. It is the year they turn fifty or forty, a major milestone in the journey of life that gets everyone asking: “So, what are we doing?” As someone born in 1988, I may not be under pressure to make a similar decision for 2027, but I am close enough to know that my turn is approaching very quickly. And truth be told, the closer I get to forty, the less interested I become in throwing a large party simply because that is what people expect. But after years of travelling, I have also realised that some of the most memorable celebrations are not necessarily the biggest. They are the ones connected to experiences. Like having a private villa breakfast which everyone will always talk about. The boat trip that almost ended with somebody losing their phone in the ocean. The birthday dinner beneath the stars. The destination everyone initially complained was too far, then refused to leave when the trip ended. That is what makes a destination party special. It does not give you one evening. It gives you several days of memories. So, if I were born in 1977 or 1987 and planning a milestone birthday for 2027, I would spend my birthday seeing the world, and these are the destination celebrations I would surely consider, even better if you’re celebrating with your friends: Bali, Indonesia You know that friendship group that has been saying, “Girls’ trip soon,” for the past five years? Every January, somebody opens the conversation again. Everyone agrees. Dates are suggested, then work happens, children happen, school fees happen, someone suddenly has a wedding; something always comes up and halts every plan. Before you know it, another year has passed. A fortieth or fiftieth birthday may finally be the excuse everyone needs, and Bali works beautifully because you can create a luxurious group experience without forcing everyone into separate hotel rooms. Imagine ten friends sharing a private villa with a swimming pool and staff. Begin with a welcome dinner. Add a spa morning, beach club, waterfalls, rice terraces and, on the birthday itself, a private chef and dinner beneath the stars. The greatest advantage of Bali is that luxury can still feel attainable. Just remember that Bali is not the place to invite people who cannot sit still. Some days, the entire plan may simply be breakfast, massage, swimming and sunset. And that is the itinerary . Private villa, poolside dinner, spa morning and sunset beach club–the perfect birthday idea. Thailand Thailand is for the celebrant who wants everything: City energy, beautiful beaches, nightlife, shopping, culture and food. item.title: Loving Itohan, Dear Ajayi & No Fury: 3 Nollywood Films to Watch in Cinemas This November
item.description: Lead stars Nancy Isime and Uzor Arukwe pose in traditional attire for Loving Itohan, arriving in cinemas this November. Photo Credit: Nancy Isime/Instagram This November, we urge you to plan your cinema itinerary well because you are about to be thoroughly entertained by Nollywood’s big-screen offerings. As the end-of-year movie season kicks into high gear, Nigerian filmmakers are serving up a rich mix of emotional romance, deeply moving historical drama, and high-stakes revenge thrillers. Whether you are stepping out for a weekend date night or gathering friends for a popcorn-filled cinematic escape, these three titles promise to make your cinema visits worthwhile. Here are the Nollywood films hitting the big screen this November. Loving Itohan If you are in the mood for a sweeping romantic drama that tests the boundaries of second chances, Loving Itohan should be at the top of your list. Executive produced by Nancy Isime , directed by Orobosa Ikponmwen , and produced by Emmanuel Izuoba , the film brings together a stellar creative team, with Lucas Oluwole capturing the vivid visual landscape as Director of Photography. Nancy Isime and Uzor Arukwe in traditional Edo attire for the romantic Nollywood drama Loving Itohan. Photo Credit: Nancy Isime/Instagram The plot follows Itohan, a woman navigating a maze of hidden truths and unexpected emotional revelations that force her to re-evaluate her understanding of love, loyalty, and past relationships. Starring Nancy Isime alongside Uzor Arukwe , Oberry Hovah , Martha Ehinome , Dorathy Bachor , Chioma Nwosu , and Grace Dein Coker, the film promises intense onscreen chemistry and compelling drama. Loving Itohan makes its nationwide cinema debut on 6 November 2026. Dear Ajayi Fresh from making waves on the international festival circuit, Dear Ajayi offers a deeply poignant, nostalgia-tinged look into 1990s Southwestern Nigeria. Directed and written by Damilola Orimogunje with KC Obiajulu as producer, this period piece centres on two estranged sisters—Ade and Titi Ajayi—who are forced back under the same roof to care for their paralysed mother. As Ade’s steadfast religious devotion collides with Titi’s rebellious spirit and musical ambitions, their tense living arrangement exposes hidden grief, familial guilt, and complex sacrifices. Lead cast members Tosin Adeyemi, William Benson, and Bimbo Akintola for Damilola Orimogunje’s period drama, Dear Ajayi. item.title: Watch Burna Boy Take Over the NFL Paris Game with a Star-Studded Halftime Show
item.description: Burna Boy backstage at Stade de France wearing a custom 3.PARADIS leather jacket look for the NFL Paris Game. Did you catch Burna Boy at the inaugural NFL Paris Game last weekend? If you missed his halftime performance at the Stade de France in Paris, we have all the details. The Nigerian Grammy Award winner took over the pitch as the Pittsburgh Steelers faced the New Orleans Saints, giving American football fans a taste of West African music. Returning to the 80,000-capacity stadium after his historic solo concert in Paris, Burna Boy opened his set with “ 4 Kampe II ”, his collaboration with French-Haitian singer Joé Dwèt Filé . He moved between English, French and Haitian Creole before welcoming French singer Yseult on stage and moving into some of his biggest hits. The set included “ On the Low ,” “ Ye ” and “ Last Last ,” with a special appearance from French judo champion Teddy Riner adding to the occasion. It was a set that gave fans in the stadium and viewers watching around the world a taste of the Nigerian star’s catalogue. Burna Boy arrives at Stade de France ahead of his halftime show performance at the NFL Paris Game in Paris. Burna Boy also made sure his outfit matched the scale of the performance. He wore custom luxury streetwear, pairing a structured oversized leather jacket with tailored cargo trousers, heavy silver neck chains and dark tinted sunglasses. The NFL Paris Game adds to Burna Boy’s growing list of major international sporting appearances. He has previously performed at the NBA All-Star Game and the UEFA Champions League Final kickoff show, taking African music to audiences well beyond the usual concert stage. The Paris weekend also coincided with the launch of his debut sneaker collaboration with Swiss sportswear brand On, under the No Giant Stands Alone campaign. Away from the stage, he was also spotted backstage catching up with French football star Paul Pogba . item.title: In Photos: Senegal Makes History as the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games Kick Off
item.description: Khaby Lame and Boubou Niang take the stage with a young participant at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony. If you have been keeping an eye on sports and global pop culture, history was made over the weekend in West Africa. Senegal officially kicked off the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games with a spectacular opening ceremony at the 55,000-capacity Stade Abdoulaye Wade in Diamniadio, marking the first time an Olympic event has ever taken place on African soil. Running through to 13 November, the Games are bringing together over 2,600 young athletes aged 14 to 17, competing across 25 sports and 153 medal events. The action spans three vibrant hubs: the historic capital city of Dakar, the modern satellite city of Diamniadio, and the coastal resort area of Saly. Host nation Senegal enters the arena during the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games Parade of Nations. Under the official motto “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates”, the opening ceremony turned into a celebration of music, dance, visual arts, and storytelling. Beyond the parade of nations, the night showcased iconic West African talent. Senegalese music legend Baaba Maal led a massive musical tribute alongside Kiné Lam and hip-hop outfit Daara J Family , while Gambian kora virtuoso Sona Jobarteh and social media star Khaby Lame made featured appearances. Massamba Gueye performs during a cultural heritage sequence at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony. Nigeria also took centre stage during the ceremony, with spoken word poet Ibukunoluwa Aramide Ajagbe , popularly known as Ibquake , delivering a live performance surrounded by dancers against a backdrop of stadium lights. Ibquake performing live at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony. The Games feature an exciting, youth-focused sports lineup including 3×3 basketball, futsal, beach volleyball, rugby sevens, breakdancing, street skateboarding, wushu, beach wrestling, table tennis, and archery. Over 200 National Olympic Committees are participating—with strong contingents representing African nations like host nation Senegal, Nigeria,South Africa, Kenya, and Algeria, alongside global delegations including Great Britain, Australia, Germany, Argentina, South Korea, and the United States. With two full weeks of sporting events, cultural showcases, and youth competition ahead, Senegal has set the tone for a historic milestone in African sports and lifestyle history. item.title: Watch Tunde Kelani’s Remastered Agogo Èèwò & Revisit the World of Saworoide
item.description: Official poster for Tunde Kelani’s remastered political classic, “Agogo Èèwò.” If you watched Saworoide , get ready to return to Jogbo. Tunde Kelani ’s political drama Agogo Èèwò (2002), the follow-up to his acclaimed classic, is now available in a newly remastered presentation on TK ÒPÓMÚLÉRÓ’s YouTube channel. Following the fall of military ruler Lagata in Saworoide, the people of Jogbo hope for a new era of peace and prosperity. But the corrupt chiefs have other plans. They install Adebosipo, played by the late veteran actor Dejumo Lewis , as the new king, believing that his background as a retired police officer will make him easy to control as they continue to exploit the kingdom’s treasury. Adebosipo, however, refuses to play along. Determined to protect the people of Jogbo, he demands accountability from the chiefs, setting off a fierce struggle over power, corruption and the future of the kingdom. The conflict reaches a defining moment during a public traditional oath-taking ceremony before the sacred Agogo Èèwò, or Gong of Taboo. Under the custom, anyone who has stolen from the land must confess before the gong sounds seven times, or face the consequences. Written by Professor Akinwunmi Isola and directed by Tunde Kelani, Agogo Èèwò remains a pointed examination of corruption, leadership and traditional systems of accountability. More than two decades after its original release, the film’s return in a remastered version gives audiences another opportunity to revisit the story and its enduring questions about those entrusted with power. The remastered Agogo Èèwò is now streaming on YouTube via TK ÒPÓMÚLÉRÓ. item.title: From Nigeria to Senegal: Ibquake Performs at Historic Dakar 2026 Opening Ceremony
item.description: Ibquake performing live at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony. Senegal came alive yesterday at the opening ceremony of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, with a vibrant celebration of culture, history and African creativity. Among the performers on stage was Nigeria’s very own Ibukunoluwa Aramide Ajagbe , popularly known as Ibquake , who represented the country with a spoken word performance. The ceremony took place at the Stade Abdoulaye Wade in Diamniadio, just outside Dakar, marking a major moment in sporting history as the first Olympic event to be hosted on African soil. More than 1,100 performers took part in the showcase, which featured music, dance, visual arts and spoken word. Senegalese music legends Baaba Maal and Kiné Lam , music group Daara J Family , Gambian kora musician Sona Jobarteh and social media personality Khaby Lame were among the other names featured. Ibquake on stage with dancers and the lit Olympic cauldron at the Dakar 2026 opening ceremony. Stepping onto the global stage in a structured white gown with a sculptural bodice and braided detailing, Ibquake performed against a backdrop of dancers in feathered and textured costumes. Her verses celebrated African identity, heritage and the possibilities ahead for the continent’s young people. Among the lines she delivered were: “We carry a flame for the African child to look beyond the horizon… We are both root and revolution.” Reflecting on the experience, Ibquake shared a personal message online about what being part of the historic occasion meant to her. She imagined her daughter one day asking when the Olympics first came to Africa, and how she would be able to tell her she was there. She wrote: “My daughter will one day ask me when the first Olympics games happened in Africa. And I’ll answer with speed and alacrity. She’ll ask me how I know… And I’ll say… Because mummy was a part of it.” Ibquake surrounded by dancers during the opening ceremony in Senegal. She went on to describe her life as a testament to God’s goodness and reaffirmed her commitment to telling African stories “Powerfully… Boldly,” adding that Africa will always be great in her eyes. The Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games run from October 31 to November 13, bringing together approximately 2,700 young athletes from 204 National Olympic Committees and the Youth Refugee Olympic Team. Competitions span 25 sports and 153 medal events, with activities taking place in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. item.title: 5 New Music Videos to Watch This Weekend: Ayra Starr, Tiwa Savage, Phyno, Ty Bello & More
item.description: Phyno and Wande Coal in the official music video for “Ndewo.” Weekend mode is officially activated, and if your playlist needs a proper refresh, the current crop of music video drops is delivering in a major way. From high-fashion pop-art concepts and heavyweight collaborations to soul-stirring worship sessions and street-hop anthems, these five releases deserve a spot on your screen right now. “Ms. Paper” – Ayra Starr featuring Theodora Ayra Starr keeps her global momentum rolling with the official music video for “Ms. Paper”, featuring French rapper Theodora from her album Starrgirl . Produced by The Elements, the track fuses sharp Afropop delivery with a seamless multilingual switch between English and French. The video leans into a brilliant, high-fashion pop-art universe built around currency motifs, retro magazine layouts, and custom toy-box packaging. Ayra shifts effortlessly through striking visual aesthetics, from a pink mini-dress with cowrie shell details to a rich blue halter top set against vibrant red hair and statement face detailing, making it a complete visual treat. “Commando” – Joshua Baraka featuring Tiwa Savage East meets West in the smoothest fashion as Ugandan singer Joshua Baraka links up with Afrobeats royalty Tiwa Savage for “Commando”, a standout cut from the Recess II project. The visualiser matches the track’s breezy, mid-tempo groove, wrapping listeners in an atmosphere of pure sonic chemistry. Joshua Baraka’s soulful R&B-infused delivery pairs wonderfully with Tiwa’s signature vocal versatility, creating a cozy, late-night vibe that is impossible to shake off. “TAFI” – TY Bello featuring Tomi Favored For those looking to slow things down and lean into a deep, meditative space, TY Bello and Tomi Favored deliver an incredible worship experience with “TAFI (Pass Over)”. Known for capturing raw, spontaneous moments of spiritual devotion, the collaboration merges TY Bello’s artistic lens and vocal depth with Tomi Favored’s soul-lifting harmonies. item.title: ONGA Celebrates Nigeria’s Diverse Food Culture with ‘Cook Your Way With ONGA’ World Food Day Activation
item.description: ONGA , the seasoning brand from Promasidor Nigeria , marked World Food Day with its three-day Cook Your Way With ONGA activation, bringing shoppers together to explore Nigeria’s diverse food cultures and celebrate the individual touches that make every meal their own. Rooted in ONGA’s Taste of Home platform, the campaign recognizes that home is not defined by one recipe or a single way of cooking. It is found in the meals people prepare their own unique way and share with loved ones, and in the everyday food experiences that bring comfort and connection. Through the campaign, ONGA is celebrating how people cook their food, not just what they cook, while highlighting its improved ONGA Chicken and Beef seasoning cubes as ingredients that make those meals enjoyable. The activation kicked off on World Food Day, Friday, October 16, and was executed through Sunday, October 18, 2026, at Jendol Ikorodu, Akasolori, on Friday; Ikeja City Mall on Saturday; and Jendol Ibeju-Lekki on Sunday. Across the three locations, shoppers explored the food cultures of Nigeria’s six regions through regional food sampling, interactive games, and culinary challenges At the ONGA Home booth, consumers experienced the taste of different homes such as Native Rice of the South-South region, Suya & Masa of the North-West region, Abacha of the South-East region, Dan Wake of the North-East region, Ofada & Ayamase of the South-West region, Jollof rice of the North-Central region, and took part in the “Cook Your Way With Onga” plate building game, which challenged them to match ingredients to a Nigerian dish against the clock. Shoppers also shared stories about what makes their food uniquely theirs, while showing off their culinary skills through a cooking competition, and had opportunities to win rewards through the several interactive experiences at the event. Speaking on the campaign, Omotayo Olaobaju , Category Manager, Culinary at Promasidor Nigeria, stated: “World Food Day Cook Your Way with Onga campaign was a fantastic platform to engage directly with our consumers online and offline. Onga believes that cooking is personal, and there is no standard recipe for great-tasting meals. Our role as a culinary partner is to inspire cooking confidence in every home ensuring that whichever recipe you choose, the improved Onga Beef or Chicken cube delivers guaranteed richness and taste She also highlighted the ongoing digital challenge as another way for consumers to participate beyond the physical activations. The celebration continues online, where consumers can take part in the Cook Your Way with Onga digital challenge for a chance to win prizes including a kitchen makeover, an iPhone 18 Pro, a fridge and other rewards by sharing their unique ways of cooking their favourite meals on www.ongatasteofhome.com . item.title: Virgin Atlantic Marks 25 Years in Nigeria – Honours Travel Partners
item.description: L-R: Georgia Mobsby, Senior Manager – Sales Excellence; Anthony Uphill, Vice President Sales; Dave Geer, Chief Commercial Officer; Yann Stirton, Country Manager – West Africa; and Liezl Gericke, Head of International, all of Virgin Atlantic, at an awards evening in Lagos celebrating the airline’s 25 years of operations in Nigeria on 22nd October 2026. British international airline Virgin Atlantic marks 25 years of operations in Nigeria with a special awards evening in Lagos, recognising the travel partners whose contributions have helped sustain and grow the airline’s presence in the country over the past quarter of a century. Held at The George Lagos Hotel on Thursday, 22 October, the event brought together Virgin Atlantic executives, travel industry partners and other stakeholders to commemorate a journey that began in July 2001, when the airline launched its Lagos service with four weekly flights operated by a Boeing 747. Speaking at the celebration, Virgin Atlantic’s Chief Commercial Officer, Dave Geer , described Nigeria as one of the airline’s most important and established markets within its international network, paying tribute to the travel partners, customers, employees and operational partners who have contributed to its success. “Technology will never replace relationships. The trust, local knowledge, and customer understanding represented in this room remain fundamental to our success,” Geer said. He also emphasized the importance of building sustainable partnerships, strengthening customer relationships and ensuring that the airline’s investments continue to support long-term commercial growth. Virgin Atlantic’s Country Manager – West Africa, Yann Stirton , acknowledged the resilience of Nigerian travel partners, particularly through periods of economic uncertainty, currency volatility and restrictions on ticket inventory. Highlighting a significant shift in the airline’s commercial performance, Stirton revealed that ticket sales in Nigeria now generate more revenue for the Lagos route than sales in any other market, including the United Kingdom. “When I arrived in Lagos in September 2023, most of the revenue on this route was sold in the UK. Today, more revenue on this route is sold here in Nigeria than anywhere else in the world,” he said. “That didn’t happen by accident. It happened because of the people in this room,” he added. Stirton thanked travel partners for their continued support through challenging market conditions and expressed confidence in building on the relationship in the years ahead. Virgin Atlantic executives and award recipients at a special awards evening held in Lagos on 22nd October 2026 to celebrate the airline’s 25 years of operations in Nigeria and recognise the outstanding contributions of its travel partners. item.title: A New Map of ‘Empty’ Space Challenges a Tranquil Picture of the Galaxy
item.description: You might imagine space to be empty. But the seeming void contains a barely perceptible fog of hydrogen and other neutral atoms. In 2020, NASA’s New Horizons spacecraft, having passed the orbit of Pluto, measured a proxy for the amount of hydrogen around it. In the area between stars in our galaxy — the “interstellar medium,” or ISM — New Horizons found around 130 hydrogen atoms per liter of space. Source

item.description: You come for the collections, take notes on the street style, and leave with a camera roll full of inspiration. That is part of the thrill of Heineken Lagos Fashion Week, there is always something exciting that makes you stop and think, “I would never have thought of that.” Rooted in cities and the cultures that shape them, Heineken finds inspiration in the people, creativity and experiences that give each city its character. Curious? And there’s still more to enjoy. Between the money-counting scenes, museum-style portrait frames, and choreography, the video keeps finding new ways to bring the song’s playful mood to life. item.title: AWIEF and Open Society Foundations Champion Women-Led Enterprises for Peace and Security in Africa at AWIEF 2026
item.description: The Africa Women Innovation and Entrepreneurship Forum (AWIEF) is pleased to announce its partnership with Open Society Foundations (OSF) for AWIEF 2026 , taking place on 10 and 11 November 2026 at the Cape Town International Convention Centre (CTICC). The annual AWIEF Conference, currently in its twelfth edition, is a flagship convening of entrepreneurs, investors, corporates, government, and development partners from across Africa and beyond. The partnership will take center stage during the opening plenary, Peace Dividends: Why Women-Led Enterprise Is a Security Strategy, Not Just an Economic One , exploring how women entrepreneurs contribute to economic stability, rebuild trust in communities affected by conflict, and help create the foundations for lasting peace. Across fragile and post-conflict regions, from the Sahel to the Great Lakes and the Horn of Africa, women entrepreneurs play a vital role in restoring livelihoods and rebuilding local markets. Yet their contribution to peace building and security remains overlooked and unsung. The plenary will examine how women-led businesses can strengthen community resilience, alongside the need for more effective access to capital, supportive policies and funding systems that empower their role in peace and development. Opening Plenary: Peace Dividends The discussion will be moderated by Idil Absiaye, Regional Head of Women, Peace and Security (WPS) Policy at UN Women , and feature: Aimée Ongeso , Program Manager, Transformative Peace, Open Society Foundations. Ibrahim Mulushewa Eshete , Co-Founder and Executive Director, Center for National and Regional Integration Studies (CeNRIS), Ethiopia. Amb. Ninikanwa O. Okey-Uche, Consul General, Consulate General of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Johannesburg. Yvette Mwanza, CEO of Kivu Mineral Resources and President of the North Kivu Chamber of Mines, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Bringing together perspectives from peace building, regional integration, diplomacy and business, the panel will explore what is working on the ground and what needs to change to better support women-led enterprises as contributors to peace and security. Through this partnership, AWIEF and OSF will spotlight the connection between women’s economic empowerment, resilient communities and sustainable peace, reinforcing the importance of recognizing women entrepreneurs as not only drivers of economic growth, but also contributors to stability across Africa. The opening plenary takes place on 10 November 2026 at the CTICC, Cape Town, as part of AWIEF 2026. Registration and tickets for AWIEF 2026 Conference are available online at: https://www.awieforum.org/purchase-conference-tickets/#tickets About AWIEF AWIEF is a leading pan-African organisation advancing women’s economic inclusion through entrepreneurship, innovation and business leadership. item.title: Tunji Olowolafe Charts Three Strategies for Research Excellence at OAU at 65
item.description: At the Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), Ile-Ife 65th anniversary celebration, Dr. Tunji Olowolafe , Founder of the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation (TOF) , called on Nigerian universities to open research to more people, test long-held beliefs with scientific rigour and carry discoveries out of the laboratory and into the economy. Speaking on the theme, Promoting Research Excellence and Innovation in Postgraduate Studies: Charting the Future, Dr. Olowolafe reframed research as the disciplined habit of correcting a nation’s course based on evidence. He described the postgraduate college as the intellectual engine room of a nation, where society sends its sharpest minds to challenge conventional wisdom and demand honest, data-driven answers. His first strategy called for opening the gates of research earlier, wider and more flexibly. He urged OAU to make its Staff Schools benchmarks for Africa, with science, technology and artificial intelligence at the core of the curriculum. He pointed to the Foundation’s Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial Community Secondary School in Are-Ekiti, which opened in September 2025 with 100 students and now has more than 170, alongside an ICT centre teaching artificial intelligence, coding, graphic design and Mandarin, with instructors teaching live from Beijing through a Starlink connection. “The postgraduate researchers of 2040 are sitting in primary classrooms today,” he said. He also questioned whether every road to postgraduate research must run through a four-year degree, inviting universities to recognize prior learning and demonstrated expertise without lowering standards. With only about one million of the two million UTME candidates admitted in 2025, he argued that flexible, digital study must become the standard model, since a digital campus needs no physical acreage. This builds on the Foundation’s Project Digi-Teach, which is training academic staff at Ekiti State University (EKSU) for digital proficiency. His second strategy urged researchers to test what society believes. Rather than dismissing indigenous knowledge without investigation or defending it without validation, he called for rigorous testing, citing Chinese scientist Tu Youyou , whose study of a centuries-old herbal remedy produced the malaria treatment artemisinin and a Nobel Prize. He extended the same principle to national history, including sensitive chapters such as the Civil War. “She neither rejected tradition nor accepted it. She tested it,” he said. The third strategy focused on pushing research out of the laboratory and directly into the economy. Dr. Olowolafe advocated university promotion structures that reward patents, commercial products and solved industrial problems alongside traditional journal publications. “Research is complete only when it leaves the laboratory and improves lives,” he said. Pointing to OAU’s exceptional tech pedigree, including Flutterwave and Moniepoint founded by its graduates, he challenged the global alumni commu

item.title: Google Pay Now Available to Visa Card Holders in Nigeria for Fast, Secure Digital Payments
item.description: Visa , one of the world’s leaders in digital payments, applauds the launch of Google Pay by participating financial institutions in Nigeria, supported through Visa’s partnership with Google . Eligible Visa cardholders of participating financial institutions can now securely add their cards to Google Wallet and make fast, convenient, and secure payments across millions of contactless acceptance points and online merchants. The launch by participating financial institutions marks another significant milestone in Nigeria’s digital payments journey, providing consumers with a simple and secure way to pay using their Android devices. By adding their eligible Visa cards to Google Wallet, users can tap to pay in stores, make purchases online, and enjoy a seamless payment experience across Google’s ecosystem. Google Pay uses tokenization technology to help protect payment information. Instead of storing or sharing a customer’s card number during transactions, a unique digital token is used, providing an additional layer of security while maintaining a fast and convenient checkout experience. As consumer demand for digital-first payment experiences continues to grow, the partnership between Visa and Google, working alongside Nigerian financial institutions, aims to support contactless payment adoption and provide Nigerians with more ways to pay securely wherever Visa contactless payments are accepted. “At Visa, we are committed to advancing the future of payments by delivering innovative, secure, and seamless payment experiences for consumers across Nigeria and beyond . Through our partnership with Google, we are pleased to support our financial institution partners as they bring Google Pay to their cardholders, combining the security of Visa’s global payment network with the convenience consumers increasingly expect in a digital-first world. Helping more people pay with confidence using their mobile devices supports digital commerce, financial inclusion, and the continued growth of Nigeria’s digital economy,” said Andrew Uaboi , Vice President and Cluster Head, Visa West Africa . “We are delighted to bring Google Wallet to Nigeria, a market at the forefront of financial innovation in Africa. Google Wallet makes everyday transactions faster and safer while removing the friction of carrying physical cards. By working alongside Nigeria’s leading financial institutions, we are expanding access to modern digital payment tools for millions of everyday consumers,” said Olumide Balogun , Country Director, Google West Africa About Visa Visa (NYSE: V) is a world leader in digital payments, facilitating transactions between consumers, sellers, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories. item.title: S.E.A CONSULTING Showcases Nigerian Craftsmanship at Design Week Lagos 2026
item.description: At this year’s Design Week Lagos , S.EA.CONSULTING brought its vision to REDESIGN AFRICA to life through an interactive exhibition that invited visitors to touch, listen, explore and connect. Presented at the National Theatre, Lagos, the installation placed local craftsmanship at the centre of a contemporary African living experience. Deep burgundy surfaces, raw tree bark, sculptural textures and a contemporary sofa from S.EA.HOMES created a setting shaped by Nigerian culture and heritage. Finishing materials were served on a dark hardwood table supported by clear acrylic bases, giving the illusion of floating wood. Guests could handle samples and discover the possibilities behind the finished spaces. Wireless headphones offered a choice of music and the founder’s statement, while a digital screen introduced the firm’s services, products, and projects. An in-house photographer captured visitors engaging with the installation, making their presence part of its story. Through this approach, S.EA.CONSULTING made a clear statement: African exhibitions should give local makers, materials and ways of living a central role. Cultural heritage offers a foundation for contemporary design that meets global standards of quality, functionality and execution. The experience connected interior architecture with sourcing, craftsmanship and everyday life, demonstrating how collaboration transforms individual products into spaces with meaning. For S.EA.CONSULTING, showing the world how we live begins with recognising the value of what we make, the stories we carry and the hands that bring our ideas to life. Rooted in culture. Built through collaboration. REDESIGN AFRICA. item.title: Eko Hotels at 50: A Defining Moment for African Hospitality on the Global Stage
item.description: The Legacy Gala & Awards night : Fifty Years of Building More Than a Hotel. Fifty Years of Building a Nation’s Hospitality Identity. 2nd of October 2026 was written in the sands of time, because some hotels are built to accommodate history, others are built to make it. For fifty years, Eko Hotels & Suites has done both. Beneath the lights of an extraordinary golden jubilee celebration, one of Africa’s most recognisable hospitality institutions made a statement that extended far beyond the walls of the magnificent Eko Convention Centre . Africa does not lack the capacity to deliver world-class excellence. What it needs are more institutions courageous enough to demonstrate it. The occasion was The Legacy Gala & Awards night, the grand celebration marking fifty years of Eko Hotels & Suites. An evening of African grandeur, international entertainment, cultural pride, distinguished personalities and extraordinary hospitality. But to describe it simply as a glamorous anniversary celebration would be to misunderstand its significance. This was not merely a party, It was fifty years of enterprise taking a bow, Fifty years of memories finding their voices, Fifty years of an institution reminding a continent that excellence is not foreign to Africa a nd for one unforgettable evening, history took attendance. A Hotel Became Part of a Nation’s Story There are buildings that occupy space, and there are institutions that occupy memory, Eko Hotels & Suites belongs to the latter. Across five decades, its corridors have welcomed presidents and policymakers, entrepreneurs and entertainers, diplomats and dreamers, international visitors and generations of Nigerian families. Within its halls, businesses have been negotiated, friendships formed, cultures celebrated, careers launched and milestones immortalized. For many, Eko Hotels is where Lagos welcomes the world, f or others, it is where the world first encounters the warmth, ambition, sophistication and extraordinary possibilities of Lagos. Yet perhaps its greatest achievement is not simply that it has remained standing for fifty years. It is that it has remained RELEVANT. In a world where brands disappear as quickly as trends emerge, longevity is an achievement. But longevity accompanied by reinvention is leadership. Eko Hotels has consistently demonstrated that hospitality must evolve beyond accommodation, It must become an experience, a cultural encounter, a n economic opportunity, a reason to travel and reason to return. Because the greatest hotels do not merely sell rooms. They give destinations a reputation worth travelling for. The Night Africa Wore Her Crown The Legacy Gala & Awards night brought together more than 1,000 distinguished guests, representing an extraordinary convergence of business, government, entertainment, culture and society. item.title: Is a job guarantee the solution to mass AI unemployment?
item.description: An old idea springs anew as a chorus of influential voices predicts that AI may trigger crises of vast magnitude In a preface to his book Capitalism and Freedom, the American economist Milton Friedman famously observed that a crisis can propel once-fringe ideas into the political mainstream. “Only a crisis – actual or perceived – produces real change. When that crisis occurs, the actions that are taken depend on the ideas that are lying around,” he wrote. The job of intellectuals, thinktanks and economists, he argued, is to refine the quality of these ambient ideas, so that good ones are ready when disaster strikes. Continue reading...

item.title: Apple Watch Ultra 4 review: longer battery life but still awaiting new features
item.description: Biggest Apple smartwatch gets better health tracking and new readiness tools with a battery and chip boost in preparation for controversial audio AI As the Ultra enters its fourth year as Apple’s biggest and beefiest smartwatch it gets the best kind of spec upgrade – longer battery life – while waiting for something potentially more transformative. That’s because several of the key features announced as part of Apple’s new smartwatch lineup for 2026 have yet to be enabled, awaiting updates towards the end of this year. That leaves the £749 (€899/$799/A$1,349) Apple Watch Ultra 4 the top dog, but basically the same as last year’s model . item.title: Labor and the Coalition are poised to take a reckless gamble on AI. Haven’t they realised community support has collapsed? | Edward Santow and Sarah Sacher
item.description: Australian workers expect the government to act to protect them from AI harms. There is a clear reform solution at hand Get our new political email , free app or daily news podcast Australia’s major political parties are edging towards rare consensus. Labor and the Coalition increasingly want to take a major bet on artificial intelligence. Yet, just as the parties are coming together, the Australian community is running the other way. Last year, only 30% of Australians believed the benefits of AI outweighed the risks. In 2026, community trust in AI appears to be falling even further. Continue reading...

item.title: Googlebook review: Google’s new laptops are woefully underbaked
item.description: Great hardware let down by software flaws on these pricey machines that combine ChromeOS with Android Google’s attempt to create a new type of laptop to compete with Windows and macOS machines is finally here, combining the best of ChromeOS and Android into the new Googlebook. With advanced links to Android phones and the best of Google built in, can these Googlebooks really compete with a MacBook Air or Surface Laptop? I took two for a spin to find out. For years, Chromebooks have been the boss of budget laptops, but Googlebooks take a different, far more premium approach. Made by a range of traditional PC makers, including Acer, Asus, Dell, HP and Lenovo, they start at £999 (€1,099/ $899 / A$2,299 ) – a far cry from the £160 Chromebooks. Continue reading...

item.title: Superbubble in the Large Magellanic Cloud
item.description: N44 is a complex nebula filled with glowing hydrogen gas, dark lanes of dust, massive stars, and many populations of stars of different ages. One of its most distinctive features, however, is the dark, starry gap called a “superbubble,” visible in this Hubble Space Telescope image in the upper central region.

item.title: Lunar Occultation of Venus
item.description: On Wednesday, June 17, skywatchers across the United States—and parts of Canada—enjoyed a rare event: a daytime lunar occultation of Venus. A lunar occultation occurs when the Moon moves directly in front of another celestial object from our viewpoint on Earth, briefly hiding it from sight.

item.title: Igniting Roman's Journey
item.description: Now on a three-month, million-mile journey to its final orbit, NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will soon reveal the universe’s darkest secrets. The mission launched at 7:26 a.m. EDT on Aug. 30 aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from Launch Complex 39A at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

item.title: August Lunar Eclipse Rises Over Louisiana
item.description: A lunar eclipse is visible over southern Louisiana. The lunar eclipse was visible throughout much of North and South America and part of Europe and Africa between Aug. 27-28. The Full Moon slipped through Earth’s shadow on Aug. 27, continuing into Aug. 28 for some parts of the world, resulting in the lunar eclipse. At maximum eclipse, the Moon takes on a dramatic dark, ruddy or coppery tint along the covered edge. New Orleans is home to NASA’s Michoud Assembly Facility, where stages for NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and structures for Orion spacecraft are produced for the Artemis missions.

item.title: Artemis III RS-25 Engine Processing: #3 Lift
item.description: Technicians prepare to transfer the #2 RS-25 SLS (Space Launch System) rocket engine (front) to the work stand with the #3 engine (back) for integration with the Artemis III core stage rocket on Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026, inside the Vehicle Assembly Building at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. During Artemis III, the four RS‑25 engines will launch the Orion spacecraft and its crew of four into low Earth orbit, generating more than two million pounds of thrust at liftoff.
